front: Q: Why is embalming a significant complication in autopsies for suspected arsenic poisoning?
back: Embalming fluids typically contain arsenic, which contaminates the body and obscures analytical evidence of criminal administration.
citation: Page 173 (Book Page): Embalming fluids contain arsenic and once the victim is embalmed, the evidence can get obscured.

category: Describe autopsy findings
front: Q: List the four classical internal pathological findings diagnostic of fatal asphyxia.
back:
1. Generalized cyanosis.
2. Visceral/vascular congestion.
3. Edema of tissues.
4. Petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu’s spots).
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): Table 13.1: General pathological changes in asphyxia: Generalized cyanosis, Vascular congestion, Edema of the tissues and viscera, Petechial hemorrhages in the skin and viscera, Fluidity of blood.

category: Describe autopsy findings
front: Q: Describe the characteristics of a typical ligature mark found in hanging.
back: Incontinuous mark, oblique direction (slanted upward), and deepest point opposite the knot location. Usually situated above thyroid cartilage.
citation: Page 152 (Book Page): Direction of the mark is oblique going upward towards the knot... well-defined groove... deepest at a point opposite to the knot.

category: Describe autopsy findings
front: Q: Contrast the facial features and ligature marks between hanging and ligature strangulation.
back: Hanging: Oblique/incomplete mark; face pale. Strangulation: Horizontal/complete mark; face intensely congested with marked petechiae.
citation: Page 153 (Book Page): Table 13.3: Hanging: Direction Oblique, Facial congestion May be present... Strangulation: Direction Horizontal, Facial congestion Marked.

category: Describe autopsy findings
front: Q: What is the first external indicator of putrefaction and its specific site?
back: Greenish-brown discoloration appearing on the right side of the abdomen (right iliac fossa) due to hydrogen sulfide.
citation: Page 136 (Book Page): Skin discoloration appears first on the right side of the abdomen... as dark brown and then green due to formation of sulfurated hydrogen.

category: Describe autopsy findings
front: Q: What volume of blood is typically required for carbon monoxide analysis at autopsy?
back: 100 cc of blood collected from the right heart, using a stoppered container to prevent evaporation.
citation: Page 160 (Book Page): Blood... 100 cc in poisoning case from right heart is specimen of choice in carbon monoxide and alcohol poisoning.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: What is the legal definition of Hurt under the Qisas and Diyat Act?
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury, or impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ without causing death.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Differentiate between Itlaf-i-Udw and Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw in chemical injuries.
back:
• Itlaf-i-Udw: Dismemberment or amputation of a limb/organ.
• Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying/impairing function, capacity, or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the badly. Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: How is the category 'Shajjah' distinguished from 'Jurh' in forensic examination?
back:
• Shajjah: Injuries specifically located on the head or face.
• Jurh: Injuries located on any part of the body other than the head or face.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw. Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face bearing mark of wound.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: A chemical burn on the scalp exposes the bone but does not fracture it. Classify this Shajjah.
back: Shajjah-i-Mudiha. This refers to a head or face injury where the bone is exposed without a fracture.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Mudiha: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Define the legal term 'Arsh' as per the Qisas and Diyat Act.
back: Compensation specified in the law for causing specific types of hurt, payable by the offender to the victim or heirs.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Arsh Compensation not is specified in law for causing hurt and by the offender to the victim or his heirs.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: What criteria define a 'Jaifah' wound under the classification of Jurh?
back: A Jurh (non-facial injury) that extends into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Classify head burns resulting in (1) non-displaced fracture and (2) displaced fracture.
back:
1. Non-displaced: Shajjah-i-Hashimah.
2. Displaced: Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement. Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Contrast Shajjah-i-Ammah and Shajjah-i-Damighah based on brain involvement.
back:
• Ammah: Fracture touches the brain membranes.
• Damighah: Fracture ruptures the brain membranes.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah-i-Ammah: Fracturing of bone and the wound touching the eas of brain. Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: How is 'Daman' determined differently from 'Arsh' for chemical burns?
back: Daman is compensation not specified in law; it is determined by the court for injuries that do not qualify for Arsh.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Daman Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court for causing hurt and payable by offender to the victim or his heirs.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Identify the subtype of Jurh Ghayr-Jaifah where skin is ruptured with bleeding.
back: Damiyah. This is a Jurh (non-facial wound) characterized by skin rupture and bleeding.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Damiyah: Rupturing of the skin with bleeding.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Hurt' as per the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance 1991.
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, or injury. Includes impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ without causing death.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of action of corrosive substances on body tissues?
back: * Destroys tissue texture on contact. * Causes chemical inflammatory reactions and ulcers. * Systemic absorption leads to vital center depression.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets, Some corrosive substances have additional systemic effects after their absorption.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Contrast Arsh and Daman regarding compensation for chemical injury.
back: * Arsh: Compensation specified in law. * Daman: Compensation determined by the court (not liable to Arsh).
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Arsh Compensation specified in law for causing hurt... Daman Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court for causing hurt.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Vitriolage' and its typical presentation in criminal assaults.
back: Throwing of sulfuric acid (oil of vitriol) to disfigure the face. Characterized by gray-to-black tissue discoloration and intense pain.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): It is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Why is gastric lavage restricted in corrosive ingestion management?
back: Strong risk of perforation of the esophagus or stomach. Corrosives soften and liquefy the mucosal walls, making tube insertion dangerous.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): It is done nearly in all cases of ingested poison except when contraindicated as in poisoning by corrosive.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Mudihah in the context of head and face injuries.
back: Hurt on the head or face where the bone is exposed but not fractured.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Mudihah: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How is a corrosive burn extending into the trunk cavity legally classified?
back: Jurh Jaifah. Applies to injuries on any part other than head/face extending into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Differentiate corrosive burns from thermal burns at the site of contact.
back: * Corrosives: Chemical staining (e.g., yellow for nitric), localized dribbling marks. * Thermal: Singeing of hair, carbonaceous deposits, vesicles containing albuminous fluid.
citation: Page 62 (Book Page): Vesicles in most cases do not appear in such burns... The lesion also shows staining on the skin and the clothes related to the type of corrosive.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Describe the characteristic external findings of nitric acid ingestion.
back: Causes yellow stains on the skin that eventually turn brown. Fuming properties often lead to additional respiratory tract irritation.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): Nitric acid behaves similar to sulfuric acid... Skin stains are yellow in color, later turns brown.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What legal term describes compensation for causing permanent organ function impairment?
back: Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw. Refers to destroying or permanently impairing the function/capacity of an organ or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How is 'Hurt' defined under the Qisas and Diyat Act?
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, or injury; or impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ without causing death.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of tissue damage in corrosive chemical burns?
back: Destruction of tissue texture at the site of contact, ranging from erythema to massive corrosion and ulceration.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets... varied appearance range from simple erythema... to massive corrosion of the tissues.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Distinguish between Arsh and Daman in chemical burn compensation.
back: Arsh: Specified compensation fixed by law for specific hurt. Daman: Compensation determined by the court where Arsh is not specified.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Arsh Compensation specified in law for causing hurt... Daman Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: A victim suffers permanent facial disfigurement from acid. What is the legal classification?
back: Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw (destroying or permanently impairing the function/capacity of an organ or causing permanent disfigurement).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-salahiyyat-i-udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What are the immediate management steps for dermal corrosive exposure?
back: Remove contaminated clothing and wash the skin thoroughly with soap and water for at least 15 minutes.
citation: Page 189 (Book Page): In case of dermal exposure... clothing should be removed, skin should be washed with soap and water and eyes rinsed with plain water for about 15 minutes.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Shajjah' as it relates to head and face chemical injuries.
back: Hurt on the head or face which does not result in dismemberment (Itlaf-i-udw) or loss of organ function.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Under the Act, what characterizes 'Jurh Jaifah' in chemical trauma?
back: A chemical injury that extends into the body cavity of the trunk (thorax or abdomen).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face... Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How do you differentiate ante-mortem from post-mortem chemical burns?
back: Ante-mortem burns show vital reaction, such as reddening (1/4 inch width) and leukocyte infiltration.
citation: Page 63 (Book Page): Heated objects and flame produce well marked reddening, 1/4 inch in width, bordering the lesion... Burnt skin shows leucocytes infiltration.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is the systemic effect of Phenol (Carbolic acid) after skin absorption?
back: Depression of central nervous system and medullary centers, potentially causing respiratory failure and coma.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): It acts systemically... depresses both higher and medullary centers especially cardiac and respiratory... causing unconsciousness and paralysis of vital centers.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Itlaf-i-udw' in the context of corrosive-induced amputation.
back: The dismemberment, amputation, or severing of any limb or organ of the body.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the body.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How does the Qisas and Diyat Act define "Hurt"?
back: Hurt is defined as causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof without causing death.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof without causing death.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What defines 'itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw' in chemical burn cases?
back: It involves the permanent destruction or impairment of the function/capacity of an organ, or causing permanent disfigurement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Contrast 'Shajjah' and 'Jurh' based on anatomic location.
back: Shajjah refers specifically to hurt on the head or face. Jurh refers to hurt on any part of the body other than the head or face.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face... Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face bearing mark of wound

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Scenario: A corrosive burn extends into the pleural cavity. What is the legal classification?
back: This is classified as Jaifah, defined as any hurt that extends into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How is 'Daman' determined for a chemical injury?
back: Daman is compensation not specified as Arsh in the law; it is determined by the court to be paid by the offender to the victim.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court for causing hurt and payable by offender to the victim or his heirs

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What are the criteria for 'Ghayr-Jaifah' chemical burns?
back: It is any hurt that does not amount to Jaifah (does not extend into a body cavity), and includes sub-types like Damiyah (skin rupture).
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Ghayr-Jaifah: Hurt not amounting to Jaifah. Damiyah: Rupturing of the skin with bleeding.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Application: A chemical burn results in the amputation of a finger. Name the legal term.
back: Itlaf-i-Udw, which refers to the dismemberment, amputation, or severing of any limb or organ.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of disfigurement, dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the body

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Differential: How does the law distinguish chemical wounds from mechanical wounds?
back: Medically both are synonymous as a "single pathological entity" (tissue break), but legally both are prosecuted under the term "Hurt".
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): From medical point of view, any break in the body tissue... is termed as wound or injury. Both words are synonymous... Law has not defined word wound so far and prefers to use the term hurt for it instead.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Arsh' as a compensatory mechanism for hurt.
back: Arsh is the specific compensation specified in law for causing hurt, payable by the offender to the victim or their heirs.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt by the offender to the victim or his heirs.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is the defining feature of 'Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah'?
back: It is a hurt on the head or face that involves fracturing a bone and its displacement.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the four primary medicolegal categories of corrosive chemical burns?
back:
1. Vitriolage (homicidal throwing).
2. Suicide (common with phenol/carbolic acid).
3. Accidental (domestic or industrial exposure).
4. Post-mortem destruction of corpses to conceal crime.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Medicolegal implication of mineral acids and alkalis is that they are mainly used as laboratory and industry chemicals and are thus accidental materials... Homicide is not possible; however, strong acid has been used to destroy the dead body of the victim to eliminate evidence of crime.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the specific medicolegal definition and motive of 'Vitriolage'?
back: The throwing of strong mineral acids (typically sulfuric acid) onto a victim. The motive is usually permanent disfigurement or blinding due to jealousy or revenge.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [It is known as oil of vitriol and is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Contrast the characteristic skin staining of sulfuric acid versus nitric acid.
back:
• Sulfuric Acid: Initially gray, turning to deep black (charring).
• Nitric Acid: Initially yellow, later turning brown.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... blackens the tissue before actual destruction. The change of color is from gray to black.] Page 177 (Book Page): [Nitric acid... Skin stains are yellow in color, which later turns brown.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the significance of 'Litmus reaction' at a burn periphery during autopsy?
back: It determines the chemical nature of the corrosive (acid vs. alkali) and confirms the burn as an antemortem chemical injury with vital reaction.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Litmus reaction at the periphery of the lesion will be in accordance with type of corrosive used.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which systemic physiological mechanism leads to death in Phenol (Carbolic Acid) poisoning?
back: Depression and paralysis of both the cardiac and medullary centers (respiratory failure) following rapid absorption through skin or mucosa.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [It depresses both vital and medullary centers especially cardiac and respiratory... Death is the most common suicidal poison.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the 'Tardieu’s spots' and their diagnostic significance in asphyxial burns?
back: Petechial hemorrhages under serous coverings (e.g., lungs/heart). They indicate capillary rupture due to anoxia, commonly seen in fuming acid inhalation.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [These petechial hemorrhages were noticed first by Tardieu and are identified with his name as Tardieu’s spots... readily seen under their serous coverings.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Why do fuming acids (Nitric/HCl) present higher medicolegal risk for respiratory death?
back: They are highly volatile; their vapors are inhaled, causing glottic edema, laryngeal stenosis, and choking (respiratory asphyxia) rather than just local skin burns.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Nitric acid... more volatile has stronger effects on the respiratory tract... Ammonia emits fumes, which intensely affect eyes and respiratory tract.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Distinguish acute oxalic acid ingestion from Cholera during forensic investigation.
back:
• Oxalic Acid: Immediate burning pain in throat, bloody vomit, rapid collapse.
• Cholera: Pain follows vomiting, characteristic 'rice-water' stools, non-acidic taste.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [No disease begins so abruptly... oxalic acid was the cause of death. No disease begins so abruptly nor on the other hand, no other crystalline poison has the strong acidic taste.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Describe the 'Vaso-vagal' mechanism of death in rapid chemical shock.
back: Acute irritation of the pharyngeal or gastric mucosa by chemicals stimulates the vagus nerve, causing sudden reflex cardiac arrest (inhibition).
citation: Page 142 (Book Page): [Inhibition of the heart through abnormal stimulation of regulatory nerves as in neuro-vagal inhibition.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the three classic chronic complications in survivors of corrosive ingestion?
back:
1. Esophageal stenosis/strictures.
2. Pyloric stenosis (stomach obstruction).
3. Laryngeal stenosis and pulmonary fibrosis.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [If the patient survives, the residual effects of such corrosions are esophageal, laryngeal and pyloric stenoses and fibrosis of the lungs.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which specific chemical substance is commonly known as "Oil of Vitriol" in medicolegal practice?
back: Sulfuric acid (commonly used in cases of vitriolage/throwing for disfiguration).
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown to disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of action of strong corrosive agents on body tissues?
back: They destroy the texture of the tissue on contact, leading to massive corrosion, inflammatory reactions, and ulceration.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets... producing different degrees of destruction to massive corrosion of the tissues.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Contrast the characteristic skin stains produced by Sulfuric acid versus Nitric acid burns.
back:
• Sulfuric acid: Gray to black stains (carbonization).
• Nitric acid: Initially yellow, later turning brown.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... It blackens the tissue... The change of color is from gray to black.] Page 177 (Book Page): [Nitric acid... Skin stains are yellow in color, which later turns brown.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the medicolegal significance of "Vitriolage" involving the face?
back: It is the intentional throwing of strong acid (usually Sulfuric) to cause permanent disfiguration, typically motivated by jealousy.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown to disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which specific chemical antidote is used for Oxalic acid poisoning to prevent absorption?
back: Calcium salts (reacts to form insoluble calcium oxalate which passes through the intestine).
citation: Page 169 (Book Page): [Calcium salt administered in case of oxalic acid poisoning reacts with it to yield poorly soluble calcium oxalate, which largely passes through intestine without being absorbed.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the characteristic autopsy findings of Carbolic acid (Phenol) ingestion?
back:
• Staining of lips and skin of face.
• White and wrinkled mucous membrane of mouth/stomach.
• Characteristic phenolic odor.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Phenol... the autopsy findings are staining of lips, skin or face, congestion and corrosion inside the mouth and stomach. ...characteristic odor.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: List three long-term residual complications (stenoses) found in survivors of corrosive burns.
back:
1. Esophageal stenosis.
2. Laryngeal stenosis.
3. Pyloric stenosis.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [If the patient survives, the residual effects of such corrosions are esophageal, laryngeal and pyloric stenoses.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Distinguish the vomitus of strong mineral acid poisoning from strong alkali poisoning.
back:
• Acid: Dark brown/black due to altered blood; causes effervescence on ground.
• Alkali: Copious, white/soapy, later becoming black.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Acid... vomits... blood stained or of dark brown color due to the presence of altered blood. The vomit will also show effervescence on contact with earth.] Page 177 (Book Page): [Alkalis... vomit is first of white color and later becomes black.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the systemic physiological mechanism of death in acute Oxalic acid poisoning?
back: Severe CNS depression, respiratory failure, and circulatory collapse leading to rapid prostration.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Oxalic acid... systemic effects after absorption are depression of central nervous system finally causing unconsciousness and paralysis of vital centers... death is due to respiratory failure.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which corrosive is identified as the most common suicidal poison in the provided text?
back: Carbolic acid (Phenol).
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Carbolic acid (phenol)... It is the most common suicidal poison.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: List the three primary strong mineral acids responsible for corrosive burns.
back:
1. Sulfuric acid
2. Nitric acid
3. Hydrochloric acid
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Strong mineral acids are sulfuric acid, nitric acid and hydrochloric acid.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: What is the primary mechanism of action for strong corrosives on body tissues?
back: They destroy the structural texture of the tissue upon contact, leading to varying degrees of destruction, from erythema to deep ulceration and massive corrosion.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets... Local lesion has varied appearance range from simple erythema... to massive corrosion of the tissues, which finally may acquire the shape of an ulcer.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Differentiate the skin staining colors produced by Sulfuric acid and Nitric acid.
back:
• Sulfuric acid: Changes tissue color from gray to black (carbonization).
• Nitric acid: Produces yellow stains that later turn brown.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... It blackens the tissue... The change of color is from gray to black. Page 177 (Book Page): Nitric acid... Skin stains are yellow in color, which later turns brown.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: In suspected corrosive ingestion, what significance do 'dribbling marks' on the chin or groins hold?
back: They indicate the victim was likely in a sitting or upright position during ingestion, allowing the corrosive to spill and burn the skin externally.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [If ingested while in sitting position, external effects are on lips, lateral aspects of chin due to irritant and dribbling effect and then on groins by dribbled solution when it falls down on thighs.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: What is the specific chemical antidote used to neutralize Oxalic acid in the stomach?
back: Calcium salts; they react with the acid to form insoluble calcium oxalate, preventing absorption.
citation: Page 169 (Book Page): [Chemical antidote... Calcium salt administered in case of oxalic acid poisoning reacts with it to yield poorly soluble calcium oxalate, which largely passes through intestine without being absorbed.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Define 'Vitriolage' and its typical legal motive.
back: The act of throwing corrosive (usually sulfuric acid) onto a person to cause permanent facial disfiguration; usually motivated by jealousy or revenge.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... It is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Why is homicidal poisoning via corrosive ingestion clinically rare?
back: The intense acrid smell and burning, unpleasant taste make it nearly impossible to administer to a conscious person unknowingly.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Homicide with phenol is rather impossible because of its intense taste and characteristic smell. ...Homicide [with strong mineral acids] is not possible because of its smell and taste.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Distinguish between postmortem blisters and antemortem corrosive burns on the skin.
back: Antemortem corrosive burns show a vital reaction (hyperemia and inflammation), whereas postmortem artifacts (like skin-slip or blisters) lack this reaction.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [The blisters burst, leaving the base moist and showing no vital reaction. These are postmortem blisters and skin-slip may wrongly be attributed to scalds.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: What are the systemic toxic effects of Carbolic acid (Phenol) after absorption?
back: It acts as a protoplasmic poison that depresses the central nervous system, particularly the cardiac and medullary respiratory centers.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [It is a protoplasmic poison, the systemic effects mainly on central nervous system. It depresses both higher and medullary centers especially cardiac and respiratory.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Which exposed body areas are most vulnerable to accidental or homicidal chemical burns?
back: Exposed skin of the face, hands, and feet, and internally the mucous membranes of the mouth, stomach, and respiratory tract.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Vulnerable sites externally are exposed areas of the body such as skin of face, hands and feet and internally mucous membranes of stomach, intestines and respiratory passages.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Define Vitriolage and its primary medicolegal motive.
back: The act of throwing corrosive (like sulfuric acid) to cause disfiguration. Motive is typically jealousy or revenge.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [It is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the local mechanism of action of corrosives on body tissues?
back: They destroy tissue texture chemically, causing destruction ranging from simple erythema to massive necrosis and ulceration.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Contrast the skin stains produced by Sulfuric acid versus Nitric acid.
back: Sulfuric acid produces gray to black charred stains. Nitric acid produces yellow stains that later turn brown.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [The change of color is from gray to black... (Nitric acid) Skin stains are yellow in color, and later turns brown.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: A victim presents with dark brown vomit and later develops pyloric stenosis. What is suspected?
back: Corrosive poisoning. The brown color is altered blood; stenosis is a long-term complication of healed corrosive lesions.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Vomiting may occur... dark brown color due to the presence of altered blood... residual effects of such corrosions are... pyloric stenoses.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Why is gastric lavage generally contraindicated in corrosive poisoning?
back: There is a severe risk of causing perforation of the stomach or esophagus due to chemical softening of the tissues.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [It is done nearly in all cases of ingested poison except when contraindicated as in poisoning by corrosive.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: List three primary autopsy findings in fatal corrosive ingestion.
back:
1. Staining/corrosion of lips and chin.
2. Congestion and corrosion of mouth and stomach.
3. Perforation of the stomach wall.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Autopsy findings are staining of lips... congestion and corrosion inside mouth and stomach. There may be perforation of stomach.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: How is the nature of a corrosive agent determined at the wound site?
back: Litmus paper testing at the periphery of the lesion identifies if the agent used was acidic or alkaline.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Litmus reaction at the periphery of the lesion will be in accordance with type of corrosive used.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Differentiate acid poisoning vomit from natural disease vomit using earth contact.
back: Vomit from acid poisoning will show effervescence (bubbling) on contact with earth; natural vomit will not.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [The vomit will also show effervescence on contact with earth in case of acid.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: How does oxalic acid ingestion cause rapid systemic death?
back: It depresses the central nervous system, causing rapid unconsciousness and paralysis of vital medullary and cardiac centers.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Remote systemic effects after absorption are depression of central nervous system finally causing unconsciousness and paralysis of vital centers.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the medicolegal significance of strong acids regarding crime concealment?
back: Homicidally, strong acids may be used to destroy the victim's body to eliminate all physical evidence of the crime.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [however, strong acid has been used to destroy the dead body of the victim to eliminate evidence of crime.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define drowning.
back: Drowning is a form of mechanical asphyxia resulting from the submersion of the nose and mouth in a liquid medium, leading to obstruction of the airway.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Level of obstruction: Nose and mouth; Type of mechanical asphyxia: Drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is drowning classified based on the presence of fluid in the lungs?
back:
1. Typical Drowning (Wet): Fluid is inhaled into the lungs.
2. Atypical Drowning (Dry): Minimal to no fluid inhalation due to laryngeal spasm.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is... mechanical obstruction of air passages from within or outside... Drowning is a form of mechanical asphyxia]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the level of airway obstruction in drowning?
back: Obstruction occurs at the nasal and oral orifices due to the liquid medium.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Nose and mouth—Drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define 'Dry Drowning' as a form of atypical drowning.
back: Death occurs from asphyxia caused by intense laryngeal spasm when water hits the vocal cords, preventing fluid from entering the lungs.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Mechanical asphyxia is... blockage of air passage from within.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is Immersion Syndrome (Vagal Inhibition)?
back: Sudden death upon entering cold water due to reflex cardiac arrest (vagal inhibition) from the impact of water on the skin or mucosa.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Carotid-sinus/vagus nerve, which gets stimulated and precipitates reflex cardiac arrest.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define Secondary Drowning (Post-Immersion Syndrome).
back: Death occurring hours to days after initial recovery from submersion, typically due to pulmonary edema, pneumonia, or electrolyte imbalances.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is important happening... which causes interference with process of oxygenation in lungs.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Describe the diagnostic significance of Diatoms in drowning.
back: Detection of silicified algae (diatoms) in closed organs (like bone marrow) indicates the victim was alive during submersion (ante-mortem drowning).
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved... especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What evidence can be found under the nails in a drowning case?
back: Contents of the drowning medium (sand, weeds, mud) may be deposited or clutched under the nails, suggesting a struggle.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [In case of drowning, contents of the water medium may get deposited under the nails.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: In a clinical scenario of drowning, what characterizes Phase II of asphyxia?
back: Struggle to breathe, deep cyanosis, engorgement of neck veins, and the development of petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu's spots).
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Phase II is characterized by struggle to breathe... Cyanosis deepens... petechial hemorrhages start appearing.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is 'Submersion of the Dead'?
back: A form of atypical drowning where a body is thrown into water after death from another cause, intended to simulate accidental drowning.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Mechanical asphyxia... when by other, is a cognizable offence... Determination of cause of death is obvious.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define Asphyxia as it relates to the process of drowning.
back: Asphyxia is an interference with the process of oxygenation in lungs characterized by struggled breathing.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is important happening during life of a person, which causes interference with process of oxygenation in lungs and its essential ingredient is struggled breathing.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is Asphyxia classified based on the cause of the obstruction?
back:
1. Mechanical (unnatural/external)
2. Pathological (disease-based)
3. Toxic (poisonous gas)
4. Environmental (oxygen lack)
5. Iatrogenic (medical procedure).
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Types of asphyxia: Mechanical, Pathological, Toxic, Environmental, Iatrogenic.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Describe the respiratory behavior seen in Phase II of fatal asphyxia.
back: Characterized by a struggle to breathe, specifically starting with the expiratory type of breathing.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Phase II is characterized by struggle to breathe, which starts with expiratory type of breathing.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What defines Phase III (terminal stage) of the asphyxial process?
back:
1. Unconsciousness/Coma
2. Shallow, gasping, specifically inspiratory-type breathing
3. Respiratory failure with heart continuing to beat temporarily.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Phase III is dominated by unconsciousness, which leads to coma. Breathing becomes irregular, shallow, gasping and mostly inspiratory type... Respiration finally fails, but the heart continues to beat for some time.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What are the five classical general pathological changes observed in asphyxia?
back:
1. Generalized cyanosis
2. Vascular congestion
3. Tissue/visceral edema
4. Petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu’s spots)
5. Fluidity of blood.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Table 13.1: General pathological changes in asphyxia: Generalized cyanosis, Vascular congestion, Edema of the tissues and viscera, Petechial hemorrhages in the skin and viscera, Fluidity of blood.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Why does blood remain fluid in deaths resulting from drowning and other asphyxias?
back: Capillary endothelium under stress secretes fibrinolysin, which prevents blood coagulation.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Capillary endothelium under stress secretes fibrinolysin, which keeps the blood in fluid state.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define 'Suspended Animation' in the context of clinical death and drowning.
back: A state where vital processes are depressed to a minimum, appearing dead but clinically recoverable; common in drowning and electrocution.
citation: Page 130 (Book Page): [Suspended animation... occurs when body vital processes are depressed to the minimum... occurrence in electrocution, drowning...]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the specific forensic value of 'Tardieu’s spots' in internal organs?
back: They are petechial hemorrhages resulting from capillary rupture due to anoxia, typically seen under serous coverings.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [These petechial hemorrhages were noticed first by Tardieu and are identified with his name as Tardieu’s spots. They occur in the substance of the organs, but are more readily seen under their serous coverings.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is drowning confirmed forensically in a decomposed body using skeletal samples?
back: Detection of diatoms within the bone marrow collected from the central part of a long bone (e.g., femur).
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Bone and bone marrow are required in... drowning. Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved... from the central part of a long bone, especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What trace evidence can be recovered from nail clippings in drowning victims?
back: Contents of the water medium (sand, mud, or organisms) deposited under the nails.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Nail clippings... In case of drowning, contents of the water medium may get deposited under the nails.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance, what legal term replaces 'injury' for body tissue breakage?
back: The term is 'Hurt'. It is defined as causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury, or impairing/disabling any organ without causing death.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Qisas & Diyat Ordinance 1991 has replaced terms of murder with qatl and injury with hurt... Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define Itlaf-i-Udw as per the Qisas and Diyat Act classifications.
back: It refers to the dismemberment, amputation, or severing of any limb or organ of the body.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the body.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What defines Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw in the context of chemical burn disfigurement?
back: Destroying or permanently impairing the function/capacity of an organ, or causing permanent disfigurement to the victim.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: An acid attack causes severe facial scarring. What is the primary classification if bone is not exposed?
back: It is classified as Shajjah, which refers specifically to hurt on the head or face not amounting to Itlaf.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face which does not amount to itlaf-i-Udw or itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How is 'Hurt' on body parts other than the head or face classified?
back: It is classified as Jurh. It is further divided into Jaifah (trunk cavity involved) and Ghayr-Jaifah.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face bearing mark of wound... Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define the term 'Arsh' in the context of the Qisas and Diyat Act.
back: Arsh is the compensation specified in the law for causing specific types of hurt, payable to the victim or heirs.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Arsh: Compensation specified in law for causing hurt payable to the victim or his heirs.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is 'Daman' and how does it differ from Arsh?
back: Daman is compensation for hurt where Arsh is not specified. The amount is determined by the court.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court for causing hurt and payable by offender to the victim or his heirs.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: If a corrosive burn extends into the abdominal cavity, what is the specific classification?
back: Jurh Jaifah. This refers to any hurt on the trunk that extends into a body cavity.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What are the three main legal terms for compensation/retaliation under this ordinance?
back: 1. Qisas (Retaliation). 2. Diyat (Blood money). 3. Arsh/Daman (Compensation for hurt).
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [amended law provides compensation for criminal hurt for the first time in the country introducing new legal terms of Daman and Diyat, in addition to Qisas.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: How is the general legal term 'injury' broadly defined in Pakistan's Penal Code?
back: Any harm caused illegally to any person in body, mind, reputation, or property.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Law also defines injury as any harm caused illegally to any person in body, mind, reputation or property.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What defines the primary action of a corrosive chemical substance on contact?
back: It destroys the texture of the body tissue it meets, leading to massive corrosion, ulceration, and inflammatory reactions.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): [Corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets... producing different degrees of destruction to massive corrosion of the tissues.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the mechanism behind the tissue blackening caused by Sulfuric acid?
back: It causes intense dehydration and carbonization, turning the affected skin from gray to black.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... blackens the tissue before actual destruction. The change of color is from gray to black.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Contrast the skin staining color of Nitric acid versus Sulfuric acid.
back:
• Nitric Acid: Yellow stains (turns brown later).
• Sulfuric Acid: Gray to black stains.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Nitric acid... Skin stains are yellow in color, later turns brown.] Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... change of color is from gray to black.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which specific medicolegal pattern indicates the victim was sitting during chemical ingestion?
back: Corrosion marks appearing on the lips, chin, and specifically on the groins or thighs due to a dribbling effect.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [If ingested while in sitting position... effects are on lips, lateral aspects of chin... and then on groins by dribbled solution when it falls down on thighs.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What simple chemical step is used at the lesion periphery to confirm agent type?
back: Litmus paper reaction testing at the edge of the corrosive lesion to determine if it is acidic or alkaline.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Litmus reaction at the periphery of the lesion will be in accordance with type of corrosive used.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the diagnostic hallmarks of Carbolic acid (Phenol) poisoning?
back:
• Characteristic phenolic odor.
• Darkening of urine on exposure to air.
• Local numbness due to anesthetic properties.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [It has a characteristic odor... Urine darkens on exposure... It acts locally... produces the sensation of heat followed by numbness.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Describe the medicolegal importance of 'Vitriol Throwing'.
back: Sulfuric acid (Oil of Vitriol) is thrown on the face to cause permanent disfiguration, typically motivated by jealousy or revenge.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [Sulfuric acid... is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Why is homicide by corrosive ingestion rare, and how is it otherwise criminally used?
back: Ingestion is rare due to intense taste/smell; criminally, strong acids are primarily used to destroy a corpse and eliminate evidence.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Homicide is not possible... because of its intense taste and characteristic smell. However, strong acid has been used to destroy the dead body... to eliminate evidence of crime.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the systemic physiological effects of Oxalic acid poisoning?
back: It acts as a CNS depressant, causing rapid prostration, weak/imperceptible pulse, and death via respiratory center paralysis.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): [Systemic effects after absorption are depression of CNS system finally causing unconsciousness and paralysis of vital centers... pulse becomes weak... and eventually imperceptible.]

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Which anatomic structures are primarily damaged by fuming corrosive acids?
back: The respiratory tract, including the nasal mucosa, larynx, and lungs, leading to choking and chemical pneumonia.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): [If corrosive substance has fuming property... Entry into respiratory passages by inhalation, affecting nasal mucosa and lungs. Effect on respiration is choking.]

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define 'Hurt' as per the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance.
back: Causing pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, or dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof without causing death.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Hurt is defined as and means causing of pain, harm, disease, infirmity, injury or impairing, disabling, dismembering any organ of the body or part thereof withoutt causing death.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What defines Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw in a corrosive burn case?
back: Destroying or permanently impairing the function/capacity of an organ or causing permanent disfigurement without amputation.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-Salahiyyat-i-Udw: Destroying of permanently impairing the function or capacity of an organ of the body or causing permanent disfigurement

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Contrast Shajjah and Jurh regarding the site of a chemical injury.
back:
• Shajjah: Hurt specifically on the head or face.
• Jurh: Hurt on any part of the body other than the head or face.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah: Hurt on the head or face... Jurh: Hurt on part of the body other than the head and face bearing mark of wound.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: A chemical burn penetrates the abdominal cavity. What is the specific legal term?
back: Jaifah. This refers to any hurt which extends into the body cavity of the trunk.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Jaifah: Hurt extending to the body cavity of the trunk.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Differentiate between Arsh and Daman in the compensation for burns.
back:
• Arsh: Compensation specified in the law for specific hurts.
• Daman: Compensation determined by the court for hurts not specified by Arsh.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Arsh: Compensation not is specified in law for causing hurt... Daman: Compensation not liable to Arsh and to be determined by the court.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What is the defining feature of Shajjah-i-Mudihah on the face?
back: Exposure of the bone without causing a fracture.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Mudihah: Exposing of bone withoutt its fracture.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define Shajjah-i-Damighah in terms of skull injury severity.
back: Fracturing of the skull where the wound ruptures the brain membranes (meninges).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Damighah: Fracturing of bone with rupturing of the brain membranes.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Distinguish Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah from Hashimah on a limb.
back:
• Hashimah: Fracturing bone without displacement.
• Munaqqilah: Fracturing bone with displacement.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Ghayr-Jaifah Hashimah: Fracturing of bone withoutt displacement. Ghayr-Jaifah Munaqqilah: Fracturing of bone with displacement.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: Define Itlaf-i-Udw regarding the loss of an organ.
back: Dismemberment, amputation, or severing of any limb or organ of the body.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Itlaf-i-Udw: Causing of dismemberment, amputation, severement of any limb or organ of the body.

category: Summarize the chemical buns as per qisas and diyat act
front: Q: What constitutes Shajjah-i-Khafifah in a chemical burn context?
back: A hurt on the head or face that does not expose the bone.
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Shajjah-i-Khafifah: Hurt withoutt exposing of bone.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What defines a corrosive lesion in clinical toxicology?
back:
- Occurs when strong acid or alkali contacts body surfaces.
- Characterized by destruction of tissue texture.
- Ranges from simple erythema to massive ulceration.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): Corrosive lesion to the skin and internal lining surfaces of the body organs occurs, when a strong acid or alkali come in contact. Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the primary pathophysiological action of strong corrosive substances on human tissue?
back:
- Destroys tissue structure upon contact.
- Causes chemical transformation of cellular components.
- May have systemic toxic effects after absorption.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): Strong corrosive substance has the property of destroying the texture of the tissue it meets. Some corrosive substances have additional systemic effects after their absorption.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: How is the type of corrosive agent differentiated during local examination?
back:
- Specific staining patterns on skin/clothes.
- Testing Litmus reaction at the lesion's periphery.
- Observation of color changes (e.g., sulfuric acid blackens tissue).
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): Litmus reaction at the periphery of the lesion will be in accordance with type of corrosive used.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Where are external burn marks typically found if a corrosive is ingested while sitting?
back:
- Lips and lateral aspects of the chin (dribbling).
- Groins and thighs (where solution falls).
- Associated with staining of worn clothes.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): If ingested while in sitting position, external effects are on lips, lateral aspects of chin due to buming irritant and dribbling effect and then on groins by dribbled solution when it falls down on thighs.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What long-term stenotic complications result from surviving a severe corrosive ingestion?
back:
- Esophageal stenosis.
- Laryngeal stenosis.
- Pyloric stenosis.
- Pulmonary fibrosis (if inhaled).
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): the residual effects of such corrosions are esophageal, laryngeal and pyloric stenoses and fibrosis of the lungs.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What are the three primary strong mineral acids encountered in forensic toxicology?
back:
1. Sulfuric acid.
2. Nitric acid.
3. Hydrochloric acid.
citation: Page 175 (Book Page): Strong mineral acids are sulfuric acid, nitric acid and hydrochloric acid.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the medicolegal significance of 'Oil of Vitriol'?
back:
- Common name for sulfuric acid.
- Thrown criminally to cause permanent facial disfiguration.
- Often associated with cases of jealousy.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): It is also known as oil of vitriol and is thrown for disfiguration of face usually in cases of jealousy.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: How is strong acid used criminally in relation to a homicide victim's corpse?
back:
- Used to destroy the dead body.
- Intended to eliminate physical evidence of the primary crime.
- Obscures identification and cause of death.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): however, strong acid has been used to destroy the dead body of the victim to eliminate evidence of crime.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: Describe the appearance of vomit in acute mineral acid poisoning.
back:
- Contains mucus and bile.
- Streaked with altered blood (dark brown color).
- Shows effervescence on contact with earth.
citation: Page 176 (Book Page): Vomiting may occur... blood stained or of dark brown color due to the presence of altered blood. The vomit will also show effervescence on contact with earth in case of acid.

category: Describe medicolegal importance of chemical burns
front: Q: What is the most common medicolegal category for mineral acid/alkali exposure?
back:
- Accidental poisoning.
- Typically occurs in laboratory or industrial settings.
- Suicide via ingestion is declining in frequency.
citation: Page 177 (Book Page): Medico-legal implication of mineral acids and alkalis is that they are mainly used as laboratory and industry chemicals and are thus accidental materials.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is drowning defined within the context of mechanical asphyxia?
back: A form of mechanical asphyxia caused by the immersion or submersion of the mouth and nostrils in a liquid medium, preventing air from reaching the lungs.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Obstruction with type of mechanical asphyxia... air passage... Drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: List the two primary classifications of drowning based on fluid inhalation.
back:
1. Wet Drowning (fluid enters the lungs).
2. Dry Drowning (laryngeal spasm prevents fluid entry).
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Mechanical asphyxia is defined as mechanical... or blockage of air passage from within.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What distinguishes 'Typical' from 'Atypical' drowning?
back: Typical drowning involves obstructive asphyxia via fluid inhalation. Atypical drowning includes death by vagal inhibition, immersion syndrome, or secondary drowning.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Mechanical asphyxia... [is] constriction of neck caused from without or blockage of air passage from within.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What finding in long bone marrow confirms an ante-mortem drowning event?
back: The presence of diatoms (unicellular algae). Diatoms enter the circulation via the lungs and deposit in distant tissues only if the heart was beating.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved... especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Why is 'Suspended Animation' clinically significant in drowning victims?
back: Metabolic processes are so depressed they appear dead, yet the victim may still be resuscitated through immediate medical intervention.
citation: Page 131 (Book Page): [Reorganization and diagnosis of suspended three is important due to its occurrence in... drowning, hypothermia and intoxication with strong hypnotic.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Which anatomical sites may trap trace evidence from the water medium during drowning?
back:
1. Under the finger nails (clippings/scrapings).
2. Inside the air passages.
3. Bone marrow (for diatoms).
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [In case of drowning, contents of the water medium may get deposited under the nails.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the mechanism of death in 'Immersion Syndrome'?
back: Reflex cardiac arrest caused by vagal inhibition upon sudden contact with cold water. It is a form of atypical drowning.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Carotid—sinus/vagus nerve, which gets stimulated and precipitates reflex cardiac arrest.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define 'Secondary Drowning' as a classification.
back: A form of atypical drowning where death occurs after an initial rescue due to pulmonary edema, infection, or biochemical imbalances.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Drowning... [is an] air passage [obstruction].]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Describe the characteristic froth found in a 'Typical Drowning' victim.
back: Fine, white, leathery, and persistent froth found at the mouth and nostrils, resulting from the mixture of air, fluid, and mucus.
citation: Page 156 (Book Page): [Autopsy findings... Lungs are edematous... there may be signs of asphyxia.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the autopsy specimen requirement for diatom analysis in drowning?
back: 2-3 grams of bone marrow from the central shaft of a long bone (ideally the femur) in a clean container.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved in a container from the central part of a long bone, especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the forensic definition of drowning?
back: A form of mechanical asphyxia caused by the submersion or immersion of the mouth and nostrils in a fluid medium, preventing air from reaching the lungs.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): Table 13.4: Water [Obstruction of respiration] -> Drowning

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is drowning broadly classified based on fluid entry into lungs?
back:
• Wet drowning: Fluid enters the lungs.
• Dry drowning: Laryngeal spasm prevents fluid entry into lungs.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is] mechanical constriction of neck caused from without or blockage of air passage from within.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Contrast the physiological mechanism of Freshwater vs. Saltwater drowning.
back:
• Freshwater: Hemodilution, hyperkalemia, and ventricular fibrillation.
• Saltwater: Hemoconcentration, pulmonary edema, and cardiac failure.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): Disturbances of both physiology and biochemistry of an individual, finally precipitating illness and even death.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Distinguish between immersion and submersion in forensic drowning cases.
back:
• Immersion: Only the face/airways are inside the fluid.
• Submersion: The entire body is under the fluid surface.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): Table 13.4: Water [Obstruction of respiration at levels of nose and mouth].

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Which specimen is collected from long bones to confirm ante-mortem drowning?
back: 2-3 grams of bone marrow from the central part of a long bone (e.g., femur) to detect the presence of diatoms.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved... especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What are the classical external diagnostic signs of a drowning victim?
back:
• Fine, white, leathery froth at mouth/nostrils.
• Presence of weeds, mud, or sand in the hands (cadaveric spasm).
citation: Page 156 (Book Page): [Cadaveric spasm] is of great value in diagnosis... establishment of the manner of death.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the primary mechanism of 'Dry Drowning'?
back: Intense laryngeal spasm triggered by small amounts of water, leading to asphyxia without significant fluid inhalation into the lungs.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): Sufficient compression to stop airflow... usual mechanism is for larynx to be lifted up so that tongue blocks back of the throat.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How is ante-mortem drowning differentiated from post-mortem immersion?
back: Ante-mortem drowning shows vital reactions: white froth, diatoms in the bone marrow, and sand/weeds in the respiratory tract or stomach.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved... in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the typical fatal period in human drowning?
back: Approximately 2 to 5 minutes, depending on the water temperature and the victim's struggle to breathe.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): Unconsciousness occurs in about one minute followed by death in two, three or at the most four minutes.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Define 'Secondary Drowning' (Near Drowning).
back: Death occurring hours or days after surviving the initial submersion, typically due to pulmonary edema, electrolyte imbalance, or infection.
citation: Page 87 (Book Page): Indirect and delayed death occurs in those cases that have non-fatal trauma. Secondary causes are therefore, results from infection.

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: At which anatomical level of the respiratory tract is drowning defined as occurring?
back: - The Lungs.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Level of obstruction ... Lungs ... drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Classify drowning based on its pathological type according to mechanical asphyxia principles.
back:
- Mechanical: Unnatural obstruction of air passages.
- Environmental: Insufficient oxygen in the inspired air.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Mechanical ... Unnatural obstruction ... Environmental ... drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Which biological marker found in bone marrow is diagnostic for ante-mortem drowning?
back: - Diatoms.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved ... to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Why is suspended animation a critical diagnostic challenge in drowning rescues?
back:
- Victim appears dead.
- Vital processes are depressed to a minimum.
- Potential for recovery exists if not miscertified.
citation: Page 130 (Book Page): [Recognition and diagnosis of suspended animation is important due to its occurrence in ... drowning]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the recommended procedure for preserving samples to detect diatoms in drowning cases?
back:
- Collect 2-3 grams of bone marrow.
- Site: Central part of long bone (usually femur).
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two to three gm. of bone marrow is preserved ... from the central part of a long bone, especially femur in case of drowning to detect the presence of diatoms.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: What is the medical definition of drowning as a type of mechanical asphyxia?
back: Obstruction of the air passages at the level of the lungs by a fluid medium.
citation: Page 150 (Book Page)-151: [Mechanical asphyxia ... Drowning ... Lungs]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: How should a medical examiner interpret post-mortem 'purging' in a suspected drowning victim?
back:
- It is a decomposition artifact.
- Putrefying gases distend the stomach.
- Forces bloodstained fluid out of nose/mouth.
citation: Page 137 (Book Page): [The postmortem purging ... in the early stages of decomposition may easily be misinterpreted as a sign of ante-mortem bleeding.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Differentiate aquatic scavenger damage from ante-mortem wounding in a recovered drowning corpse.
back:
- Scavengers (fish/crabs) cause bite marks/tearing.
- Lacks vital reaction.
- Often involves evisceration of body cavities.
citation: Page 140 (Book Page): [Fish and crabs under water precipitate ravage and cause bites marks and tearing ... may simulate ante-mortem injuries]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: Why does blood typically remain in a fluid state in acute asphyxial drowning?
back: Capillary endothelium under stress secretes fibrinolysin, which lyses clots.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Capillary endothelium under stress secretes fibrinolysin, which keeps the blood in fluid state.]

category: Define and classify drowning
front: Q: List the four classic pathological hallmarks of asphyxia observed in drowning autopsies.
back:
- Generalized cyanosis.
- Vascular congestion.
- Tissular edema.
- Petechial hemorrhages (Tardieu's spots).
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [General pathological changes in asphyxia ... Generalized cyanosis ... Vascular congestion ... Edema ... Petechial hemorrhages]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What is the level of obstruction in drowning according to mechanical asphyxia classification?
back: The level of obstruction is the 'Level of Respiration.'
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Level of obstruction with type of mechanical asphyxia... Water (Drowning)... Level: Level of respiration.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What is the primary pathophysiology of 'Dry Drowning'?
back: Intense laryngeal spasm occurs when water hits the larynx, preventing water from entering lungs, resulting in death via pure asphyxia.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is... interference with process of oxygenation in lungs and its essential ingredient is struggled breathing.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Define the mechanism of 'Wet Drowning.'
back: Inhalation of fluid into the air passages, leading to pulmonary interference and electrolyte imbalances.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Water (Drowning)... Level: Level of respiration.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Describe the electrolyte shift in Freshwater (Wet) Drowning.
back: Hypotonic water enters circulation → Hemodilution → Hemolysis → Hyperkalemia.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Biochemistry of fatal asphyxia is more relevant... exchange of sodium and potassium ions across cell membrane.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What is the terminal cardiac mechanism in Freshwater Drowning?
back: Hyperkalemia and massive hemodilution lead to ventricular fibrillation within 4-5 minutes.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Biochemistry of fatal asphyxia... atmosphere of the cell is conducive to its death.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of Saltwater (Wet) Drowning.
back: Hypertonic water in alveoli draws plasma from blood → Acute pulmonary edema → Hemoconcentration → Cardiac failure.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Anoxia also increases permeability of capillary wall forcing fluid out into the tissue spaces and this transudation of plasma... cause edema.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What is the mechanism of 'Immersion Syndrome' (Reflex Cardiac Arrest)?
back: Sudden cold water contact stimulates the vagus nerve, causing instant reflex cardiac standstill (Vagal Inhibition).
citation: Page 150 (Book Page): [Pressure on carotid sinus/vagus nerve, which stimulated and precipitates reflex cardiac arrest.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What defines 'Secondary Drowning' (Post-Immersion Syndrome)?
back: Death occurring minutes to days after apparent rescue due to chemical pneumonitis, pulmonary edema, or respiratory failure.
citation: Page 155 (Book Page): [If the victim survives, he may take one of two possible courses: irreversible cerebral ischemia... or reversible.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Describe Phase I of the drowning process (Asphyxial Phase).
back: Initial struggle and deep inspiration followed by stimulation of the respiratory center, increasing rate and amplitude.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Phase I initiates stimulation of respiratory center increasing both rate and amplitude of respiratory movement.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Why is drowning considered a state of 'Suspended Animation'?
back: Body processes are depressed to a minimum, making the victim appear dead though resuscitation is still possible.
citation: Page 141 (Book Page): [Suspended animation... occurrence in electrocution, drowning, hypothermia.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: How is Drowning primarily classified as a cause of death?
back: It is a form of Mechanical Asphyxia caused by the obstruction of the respiratory tract by fluid.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Obstruction with type of mechanical asphyxia ... Lungs / Drowning]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: What is the defining physiological mechanism of 'Wet Drowning'?
back: Inhalation of fluid into the lungs, leading to mechanical obstruction of the air passages and systemic anoxia.
citation: Page 149 (Book Page): [Asphyxia is... interference with process of oxygenation in lungs and its essential ingredient is struggled breathing.]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Explain the primary mechanism of death in 'Dry Drowning.'
back: Death occurs due to intense laryngeal spasm triggered by water contact, preventing fluid from entering the lungs but causing immediate asphyxia.
citation: Page 151 (Book Page): [Table 13.4: Larynx and upper trachea / Choking ... Drowning]

category: Explain mechanism of death in wet and dry drowning
front: Q: Which reflex mechanism causes rapid death in cold water immersion before inhalation?
back: Vagal Inhibition (reflex cardiac arrest) caused by stimulation of the carotid sinus or laryngeal nerves by cold fluid.
