citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Appearance of stria-gravidarum... Skin pigmentation (from pubis to umbilicus).]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the characteristic findings of the uterus in the abdomen immediately after delivery?
back: The uterus is palpable as a hard globe approximately five inches above the symphysis pubis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [The uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the physiological regression of the fundus following delivery.
back: The fundus remains palpable above the pubis until it sinks behind it around the tenth day.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the composition of lochia in the first 4 days versus the 10th day postpartum.
back:
First 4 days: Sanguineous (blood-stained). 
10th day: Becomes serous, offensive, and white in color.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [This discharge is blood stained for first four days and then it becomes serous, offensive and white in color about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Internal Signs of Delivery in the Dead
front: Q: In a forensic autopsy, what internal findings in the ovaries confirm recent delivery?
back: The presence of a corpus luteum in one of the ovaries.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding during autopsy is corpus luteum in one of the ovaries.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Until what gestational month is the corpus luteum typically identifiable during autopsy?
back: It is identifiable up to the fifth month of gestation.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [It is found up-to ten days after its formation and if available up-to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What specific feature of the inner uterine surface is sought during autopsy to prove delivery?
back: Signs of the site of placental detachment.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How is the state of the abdominal wall described in a recent delivery case?
back: The abdominal wall is typically lax.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are that-abdomen is lax.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Birth Canal Trauma in Forensic Delivery
front: Q: What local injuries to the birth canal serve as signs of a recent delivery?
back: Tears and injuries involving the vagina and cervix.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina...]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Recent vs. Old Signs of Delivery
front: Q: Why do "remote" signs of delivery lose forensic importance compared to "recent" signs?
back: Because recent signs disappear or are modified as the time duration since delivery increases.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Define the primary diagnostic indicators for Proof of Delivery according to the text.
back: Signs of full-term pregnancy modified by whether the delivery event was recent or remote.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Proof of delivery will depend upon signs of full term pregnancy modified by event of delivery whether recent or remote.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the position of the uterus immediately after a recent delivery in a living woman?
back:
* Palpable as a hard globe
* Situated approximately five inches above the pubis
* Sinks behind the pubis by the tenth day
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the three stages of Lochia discharge following recent delivery.
back:
* First 4 days: Blood-stained
* Until 10th day: Pale brown or yellow
* After 10th day: Offensive white (alba)
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): This discharge is blood stained for first four days, and then becomes pale brown or yellow up-to the tenth day. Additional finding, during autopsy, is presence of corpus luteum

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of abdominal striae in recent versus old delivery.
back:
* Recent: Striae gravidarum (pinkish/bluish lines)
* Old: Striae albicantes (silvery-white permanent scars)
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Appearance of stria-gravidarum... Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Autopsy Finding: A woman has a corpus luteum in the ovary. How long does this persist post-delivery?
back:
* Identifiable up to 10 days after formation
* Persists to the fifth gestational month if pregnancy continues
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): presence of corpus luteum... up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnancy continues to the fifth gestational month.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What internal uterine marker indicates a recent delivery during a medicolegal autopsy?
back: * The inner surface of the uterus shows signs of placental detachment at the placental site.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta at placental site.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the primary signs of old (remote) delivery in a living woman's genitalia?
back:
* Perineal or vaginal scars (from old tears)
* Cervical os appears as a transverse slit rather than circular
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Inferred from Signs of Remote Event] ...modification/disappearance of signs of recent event... [and] transverse slit appearance of cervical os.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the abdominal wall change from a recent to an old delivery state?
back:
* Recent: Lax and wrinkled wall
* Old: Remains loose/lax but striae turn silvery (albicantes)
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Skin at-abdomen is lax, and shows stria-gravidarum.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Differential: A victim has white discharge 11 days post-alleged delivery. What is the diagnosis?
back:
* Lochia Alba
* Indicates delivery occurred approximately 10-14 days prior
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Lochia] becomes offensive and white in color after tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What breast changes are characteristic of a recent delivery in the living?
back:
* Presence of colostrum or milk
* Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles
* Breasts are full and firm (later flabby in old cases)
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... Signs in breasts [include] Gradual enlargement.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the forensic significance of the internal size of the uterus post-mortem?
back: * The length and width of the uterus are used to estimate the specific gestational month of the recent pregnancy.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): The size of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Where is the uterine fundus palpable immediately after a recent delivery?
back: Palpable as a hard globe about five inches above the pubis. It sinks behind the pubis usually by the tenth day.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the characteristic color progression of 'lochia' in the first ten days post-delivery.
back:
* First 4 days: Blood-stained (Lochia Rubra).
* Until 10th day: Becomes serous, then white and offensive (Lochia Alba).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [discharge called lochia. This discharge stays blood-stained for first four days and becomes serous and white in color and offensive by the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the fresh abdominal signs of a recent delivery in a living woman?
back:
* Abdomen is lax and soft.
* Fresh 'striae gravidarum' (reddish/purplish lines).
* Linea nigra (pigmentation from pubis to umbilicus).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [at-abdomen is lax, and skin-pigmentation (from pubis to umbilicus). Appearance of stria-gravidarum]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Identify the specific internal uterine finding during an autopsy that confirms recent delivery.
back: The internal surface of the uterus shows signs of placental detachment, appearing as a raw area with clotted blood.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding, during autopsy... Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the corpus luteum assist in diagnosing recent delivery at autopsy?
back: A large 'corpus luteum of pregnancy' is found in the ovary, persisting up to ten days post-delivery.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [presence of corpus luteum in non-pregnant ovary up-to ten days after its formation]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of the external os in a nulliparous vs. a multiparous woman.
back:
* Nulliparous: Small, circular opening.
* Multiparous (Old delivery): Transverse slit or jagged, irregular opening.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event... External os of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy (multiparous)]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What breast findings suggest delivery has occurred within the last few days?
back:
* Breasts are enlarged and firm.
* Presence of colostrum or milk.
* Prominent Montgomery’s tubercles and pigmented areolae.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs in breasts: Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... presence of milk or colostrum]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: A woman claims her first delivery was years ago. What abdominal sign confirms this?
back: Presence of 'striae albicantes', which are silvery-white, shriveled, permanent scars from previous tissue stretching.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event... shriveled silvery-white scars called striae-albicantes on abdomen.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the diagnostic injuries to the birth canal in a recent full-term delivery?
back:
* Tears of the fourchette or perineum.
* Bruising and swelling of the vulva.
* Soft, dilated, and often lacerated cervix.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina... vulva is swollen and bruised]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does uterine weight at autopsy differentiate a recent delivery from a nulliparous state?
back:
* Nulliparous: 40-50 grams.
* Post-delivery: Approximately 900-1000 grams (gradually decreasing during involution).
citation: Page 122 (Book Page): [UTERUS: Weight in nullipara... 40-50 (gm). Weight after delivery... 900-1000 (gm).]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Where is the uterus palpable in the living immediately following a recent delivery?
back: It is felt as a hard globe approximately five inches above the symphysis pubis. It typically sinks behind the pubis by the tenth day.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the color and odor progression of lochia during the first ten days post-delivery.
back:
• First 4 days: Blood-stained.
• Days 5-9: Greenish and offensive.
• Day 10: Becomes white.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [This discharge remains blood stained for first four days, then becomes greenish/offensive and white in color by tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the primary internal uterine findings during an autopsy for recent delivery?
back:
• Inner surface shows placental detachment sites.
• Uterine size corresponds to the specific stage of pregnancy or postpartum interval.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta and size of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: In a decomposed corpse, why is the uterus significant for identifying past delivery/pregnancy?
back: The non-gravid uterus is a compact organ with dense fibrous tissue; it resists putrefaction and remains recognizable after other soft organs decompose.
citation: Page 137 (Book Page): [Prostate and non-gravid uterus being compact organs having dense fibrous tissue remains recognizable when decomposition of all other organs has far advanced.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the significance of the corpus luteum in a non-pregnant state during autopsy?
back: It serves as a diagnostic indicator of recent delivery, persisting in a non-pregnant state for up to ten days after its formation.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding during autopsy is corpus luteum in non pregnant state up-to ten days after its formation.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What objective skin and abdominal changes indicate a recent delivery in the living?
back: The abdomen appears characteristically lax with soft skin, frequently accompanied by localized pigmentation.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Abdomen is lax, skin soft and pigmented.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the defining characteristic of 'remote' or old signs of delivery.
back: Remote signs lose diagnostic importance over time as recent indicators (lochia, fresh tears) disappear or undergo modification.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Which breast changes serve as objective indicators of pregnancy or recent delivery?
back:
• Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles.
• Increased skin pigmentation (areolar).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... Skin pigmentation (from pubis to umbilicus)]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How is the vaginal canal affected immediately following a full-term delivery?
back: The birth canal often shows fresh tears or lacerations in the vaginal wall and introitus.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What defines the physical state of the uterus in the first few days post-delivery?
back: It is palpable as a firm, hard globe, reflecting its initial stage of involution.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the breast changes in a woman who has recently delivered?
back:
* Enlarged, firm, and pendulous appearance.
* Primary and secondary areolae are deeply pigmented.
* Colostrum or milk can be expressed on squeezing.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are... breasts are enlarged and pendulous. Primary and secondary areolae are pigmented... colostrum or milk.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the sequence and color changes of lochia following recent delivery.
back:
* First 4 days: Lochia rubra (blood-stained).
* 5-9 days: Lochia serosa (pale/serous).
* After 10 days: Lochia alba (white and offensive).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [specific vaginal discharge called lochia. This discharge remains blood stained for first four days... becomes pale and offensive and white in color after tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What internal uterine findings during autopsy indicate a recent delivery?
back:
* Uterus is a palpable hard globe.
* Inner surface shows signs of placental site detachment.
* Presence of a corpus luteum in the ovary.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe... Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta. Presence of corpus luteum... up-to ten days after its formation.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the external os of the cervix differentiate a remote delivery from a nulliparous state?
back:
* Nulliparous: Circular and small.
* Remote Delivery: Transverse, slit-like, or irregular due to healed tears (parous os).
citation: Page 94 (Book Page): [Inability to perform sexual intercourse... parous os.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Differentiate between the abdominal striae seen in recent versus remote delivery.
back:
* Recent: Striae gravidarum (reddish or purple lines).
* Remote: Striae albicantes (silvery-white, permanent scars).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Appearance of stria-gravidarum... Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the position of the uterine fundus immediately versus ten days after delivery.
back:
* Immediate: Hard globe five inches above the pubis.
* Tenth Day: Sinks behind the symphysis pubis (no longer palpable abdominally).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What changes occur in the vaginal canal immediately following a recent delivery?
back:
* Canal is lax and dilated.
* Mucosal rugosities are lost or smoothed out.
* Presence of fresh tears or fourchette lacerations.
citation: Page 103 (Book Page): [Digital examination... difference of tone and extent of rugosities... rugosities are lost in the habituated vagina along with proportionate dilatation.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the significance of the corpus luteum in delivery status during autopsy?
back:
* Identifiable up to 10 days post-delivery in non-pregnant states.
* Persists up to the fifth gestational month if pregnancy occurred.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding during autopsy is of corpus luteum... up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnancy occurs up-to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: List the external signs indicating a woman has delivered in the remote past.
back:
* Silvery striae albicantes on abdomen.
* Healed scars on the perineum or fourchette.
* Labia majora gape and are less firm.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How is the placental site identified in a recently delivered uterus at autopsy?
back:
* Internal surface of the uterus is rough and dark.
* Shows signs of detachment where the placenta was fixed.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta. Inner surface of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the characteristic abdominal skin findings in a female with recent delivery?
back:
• Abdominal wall is lax and flaccid.
• Linea nigra (pigmentation) is prominent.
• Striae gravidarum appear as fresh, reddish or pinkish streaks.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are that-abdomen is lax, palpable as a hard globe... Skin pigmentation... Appearance of stria-gravidarum]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Define the characteristic stages and colors of lochia following recent delivery.
back:
• Lochia Rubra: Freshly blood-stained, first 1–4 days.
• Lochia Serosa: Paler, serous discharge, 5th to 9th day.
• Lochia Alba: White or purulent, from 10th day onwards.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [specific vaginal discharge called lochia. This discharge remains blood stained for first four days (lochia rubra), becomes paler (lochia serosa)... white in color (lochia alba) from tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does uterine involution progress in the living during the first 10 days post-delivery?
back:
• Immediately: Palpable as a hard globe 5 inches above the symphysis pubis.
• By 10th Day: Sinks behind the pubis and is no longer palpable abdominally.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the specific findings in the birth canal during an examination for recent delivery?
back:
• Vulva and vagina are edematous and bruised.
• Presence of fresh lacerations or tears in the perineum and vaginal walls.
• Hymen is freshly ruptured.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina...]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What permanent change occurs to the external cervical os after a vaginal delivery (Remote Signs)?
back:
• Changes from a circular opening (nulliparous) to a transverse or irregular slit.
• Healed fissures or scarring may be visible on the margins.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What defines the placental site appearance during a forensic autopsy for recent delivery?
back:
• Uterine inner surface shows a shaggy, dark, and congested area.
• Measures approximately 3 to 4 inches in diameter at the site of detachment.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta... shaggy, dark and congested area of 3-4 inches in diameter.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the significance of the corpus luteum finding during an autopsy for recent delivery.
back:
• A large corpus luteum of pregnancy is present in one ovary.
• It typically persists and remains prominent up to the 5th gestational month.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding, during autopsy, is presence of corpus luteum... up-to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the breast findings in recent versus remote delivery.
back:
• Recent: Enlarged, tense, Montgomery’s tubercles prominent, secreting colostrum/milk.
• Remote: Breasts less firm (flabby), striae albicantes (silvery-white scars), nipples darker.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... secretions... Page 96 (Book Page): Signs of remote event depend upon... modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: In a dead body, what uterine measurements suggest a remote (old) delivery?
back:
• Uterus is permanently larger and heavier than a nulliparous uterus.
• Uterine cavity is increased in size.
• Uterine walls are thicker and more fibrous.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment... weight of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: A woman claims delivery 2 weeks ago; why might vaginal examination findings be inconclusive?
back:
• Lochia alba (white discharge) replaces blood-stained lochia after day 10.
• Uterus has already sunk behind the symphysis pubis.
• Edema and fresh bruising of the vulva have typically subsided.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day... lochia... white in color (lochia alba) from tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the three stages and typical colors of lochia after recent delivery?
back:
- Lochia Rubra: Blood-stained (Days 1-4).
- Lochia Serosa: Pale/serous (Days 5-9).
- Lochia Alba: White/offensive (By Day 10).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Lochia. This discharge remains blood stained for first four days, then becomes serous and later offensive and white in color by the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the uterine involution process in the first ten days post-delivery.
back:
- Immediately: Palpable hard globe ~5 inches above pubis.
- Day 10: Progressively sinks and becomes hidden behind the pubic symphysis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of abdominal striae in recent versus remote delivery.
back:
- Recent: Red or purple pigmented streaks (striae gravidarum).
- Remote: Silvery-white scars (striae albicantes).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page)-96: [Skin pigmentation... Appearance of stria-gravidarum... Signs of remote event... striae albicantes.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: A woman claims delivery 15 days ago; what abdominal finding disproves this claim?
back: If the uterus is still palpable above the pubis, it disproves the claim; it should sink behind the pubis by day 10.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus... sinks behind pubis about the tenth day. Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the internal Os appearance differ in nulliparous versus multiparous states?
back:
- Nulliparous: Circular and smooth.
- Multiparous: Transverse, slit-like, or irregular due to previous delivery-related tears.
citation: Page 94 (Book Page): [Inability to perform sexual intercourse... Os is transverse/slit-like (for remote delivery).]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: List three primary breast changes diagnostic of recent delivery.
back:
- Breast enlargement and increased firmness.
- Montgomery's tubercles become prominent.
- Secretion of colostrum or milk on expression.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs in breasts: Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... Increase in secretions.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: In a postmortem examination, what ovarian and uterine findings confirm recent delivery?
back:
- Ovary: Presence of a large corpus luteum.
- Uterus: Inner surface shows a raw, ragged placental attachment site.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Corpus luteum... up-to the fifth gestational month. Inner surface of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast vaginal rugosities in nulliparous women versus those with a history of delivery.
back:
- Nulliparous: Prominent and distinct rugosities.
- Multiparous/Remote Delivery: Rugosities are flattened, lost, or smoothed out.
citation: Page 103 (Book Page): [The difference of tone and extent of rugosities is an index to differentiate habituated vagina... The rugosities are lost in the habituated vagina.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the significance of the 'Placental Site' during a forensic autopsy.
back:
- Appearance: A raw, ragged area inside the uterus.
- Significance: Confirms the exact site of placental detachment and recent pregnancy termination.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of the placenta. Size of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the weight of the uterus immediately and one week after delivery?
back:
- Immediately: Approx. 2 lbs (900-1000g).
- One week: Approx. 1 lb (500g).
citation: Page 122 (Book Page): [Weight after childbirth 700-1230 gm (Table 11.4).]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: What physical changes characterize the abdominal wall immediately following a recent delivery?
back: - The abdominal wall becomes lax and wrinkled.- Presence of fresh, reddish-purple striae gravidarum (stretch marks).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Sign of recent event are that abdomen is lax, wrinkled and show stria-gravidarum.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: How is uterine height used to estimate the time elapsed since delivery?
back: - Immediately post-delivery: Palpable as a hard globe ~5 inches above the pubis.- By the 10th day: Sinks behind the pubic symphysis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Describe the chronological changes in lochia during the first ten days postpartum.
back: - Days 1-4: Blood-stained discharge.- Days 4-8: Serous/pale discharge.- After Day 10: Offensive and white in color.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [specific vaginal discharge called lochia. This discharge initially is blood stained for first four days, then serous and offensive and white in color after tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Ovarian Indicators of Delivery or Pregnancy
front: What is the significance of a corpus luteum found during autopsy in a suspected delivery case?
back: - In a non-pregnant state post-delivery, it persists for up to ten days.- During pregnancy, it remains until the fifth gestational month.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding during autopsy is corpus luteum in non-pregnant state persists up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnant up to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Which internal uterine findings at autopsy confirm a recent delivery?
back: - Signs of placental detachment on the inner uterine surface.- Uterine size and weight that correlate with the suspected stage of gestation or involution.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta and size of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Birth Canal Trauma in Recent Delivery
front: What injuries to the birth canal are commonly observed after a recent delivery?
back: - Fresh tears or lacerations of the vagina and vulva.- General bruising and dilation of the vaginal walls.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Which breast examination findings provide evidence of a recent or full-term delivery?
back: - Enlargement of the breasts and Montgomery's tubercles.- Presence of colostrum or milk secretions.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [signs of full term pregnancy... enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles... secretion in the breasts.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Remote vs. Recent Signs of Delivery
front: Why do 'remote' or 'old' signs of delivery lose their forensic importance over time?
back: - Recent signs (lochia, lax abdomen) disappear within weeks.- Old signs (healed scars) are modified or less specific for timing past events.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Describe the physical state of the uterus immediately following delivery.
back: The uterus is a hard, globular, and firm mass palpable approximately 5 inches (12.5 cm) above the symphysis pubis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: What is the primary indicator of placental site presence during a forensic autopsy?
back: A raw, ragged area on the inner surface of the uterus where the placenta was previously attached.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: List three primary external signs of recent delivery in a living woman.
back:
- Lax, wrinkled abdominal wall.
- Pinkish-red striae gravidarum.
- Enlarged breasts with prominent Montgomery’s tubercles and colostrum.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are that-abdomen is lax, wrinkled having pinkish-red striae-gravidarum... Breast are enlarged having prominent Montgomery’s tubercles.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the stages and duration of lochial discharge following delivery.
back:
- Lochia Rubra: Blood-stained (first 4 days).
- Lochia Serosa: Pale/serous (next 2-3 days).
- Lochia Alba: White/offensive (until 10th-14th day).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [This discharge initially blood stained for first four days (lochia-rubra), then becomes pale for next two to three days (lochia-serosa) and finally offensive and white in color (lochia-alba) upto tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Contrast the appearance of striae in recent vs. old delivery.
back:
- Recent: Striae gravidarum are pinkish-red or purple.
- Old: Remote signs involve the disappearance of recent color, leaving silvery-white scars (striae albicantes).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are... wrinkled having pinkish-red striae-gravidarum... Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Why is the uterus valuable for identifying delivery status in decomposed remains?
back: The non-gravid uterus is composed of dense fibrous tissue, making it highly resistant to putrefaction and recognizable even after other soft tissues liquefy.
citation: Page 137 (Book Page): [Prostate and non-gravid uterus being compact organs having dense fibrous tissue remains recognizable when decomposition of all other organs has far advanced.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the height and involution of the uterus during the first ten days postpartum.
back: Immediately after delivery, the uterus is a hard globe 5 inches above the pubis. It typically involutes to sink behind the pubis by the tenth day.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: State the diagnostic criteria for a placental site during a forensic autopsy.
back: The inner uterine wall shows a rough, elevated area at the site of placental attachment, typically involving detached membranes and clotted blood.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner wall of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy showing signs of detachment of placenta.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What evidence of delivery is found in the ovaries during autopsy?
back: The presence of a corpus luteum of pregnancy, which persists until the fifth month of gestation and for approximately ten days after delivery.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding during autopsy is corpus-luteum in non-pregnant state persists up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnancy occurs up-to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Differentiate recent delivery from a pelvic tumor in a dead body.
back: Delivery shows a placental attachment site, lochia, and a corpus luteum in the ovary; tumors lack these physiological signs of gestation.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner wall of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy showing signs of detachment of placenta... corpus-luteum in non-pregnant state persists up-to ten days.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the internal os change immediately following delivery?
back: In a recent delivery, the internal os and cervical canal remain patulous (open), typically admitting two or more fingers for several days.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are that-abdomen is lax... Uterus is palpable as a hard globe... Inner wall of uterus... showing signs of detachment of placenta.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Define the anatomic features of an 'old' or remote delivery.
back:
- Pendulous, flabby breasts.
- Darkened areolae.
- Silvery striae albicantes on the abdomen.
- Old healed scars on the perineum or cervix.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the characteristic findings of the uterus in the immediate post-delivery state?
back:
* Palpable as a hard globe
* Positioned approximately five inches above the symphysis pubis
* Sinks behind the pubis by the tenth day post-delivery
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs of recent event are that-abdomen is lax, uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the clinical progression and characteristics of Lochia in a recent delivery case.
back:
* Days 1-4: Primarily blood-stained discharge
* Days 4-10: Becomes serous
* After Day 10: Offensive and white in color
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [a specific soiling discharge called lochia. This discharge remains blood stained for first four days, then serous, offensive and white in color after tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: During an autopsy of a suspected recent delivery, what specific uterine findings are characteristic?
back:
* Presence of a placental site on the inner uterine surface
* Evidence of recent detachment of the placenta
* Enlarged uterine size and weight relative to nulliparous state
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Additional finding, during autopsy is corpus luteum... Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta. Size of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How long does the Corpus Luteum persist at autopsy in pregnant versus non-pregnant states?
back:
* Non-pregnant: Persists up to ten days after formation
* Pregnant: Persists until the fifth gestational month
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [corpus luteum in non-pregnant state persists up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnant up to the fifth gestational month.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What external abdominal findings differentiate a remote (old) delivery from a nulliparous state?
back:
* Laxity of the abdominal wall
* Presence of Linea Albicantes (silvery white striae)
* Persistence of skin pigmentation from pubis to umbilicus
citation: Page 94 (Book Page): [Skin pigmentation (from pubis to umbilicus). Appearance of stria-gravidarum.] Page 95 (Book Page): [At-abdomen is lax... Signs of remote event depend upon time duration.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: In a clinical scenario, which breast changes suggest a prior history of full-term pregnancy?
back:
* Enlargement and persistence of Montgomery’s tubercles
* Darkened areolar pigmentation
* Presence of secondary areola
citation: Page 94 (Book Page): [Signs in breasts... Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How does the external os of the cervix differ between a nulliparous and parous woman?
back:
* Nulliparous: Circular or small transverse opening
* Parous: Transverse slit with irregular, scarred, or torn margins
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina.] Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the internal autopsy indicators for remote (old) delivery in the pelvic organs?
back:
* Increased uterine weight (100-120g vs 40-50g in nullipara)
* Uterine cavity is larger and more triangular
* Prominent, thickened uterine vessels
citation: Page 122 (Book Page): [UTERUS Weight in nullipara.... 40-50 gm. Weight after a birth 100-120 gm.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Compare the vaginal rugosities in a recently delivered woman versus one who delivered remotely.
back:
* Recent: Rugosities are almost completely obliterated/flattened due to massive distension
* Remote: Rugosities partially reappear but remain less prominent than in a virgin
citation: Page 94 (Book Page): [Changes in the vagina... Increase in secretions... Thinning of mucosa.] Page 103 (Book Page): [Rugosities are marked in virgins and flatten proportionate to the number of sexual acts... get almost obliterated.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: List the two primary components required to confirm delivery in a living person.
back:
* Subjective history provided by the female
* Objective findings (fundal height, lochia, vaginal tears, abdominal laxity)
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Proof of pregnancy depends upon subjective history by female and objective findings observed during medical examination... Proof of delivery will depend upon signs of full term pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the characteristic findings of Lochia in the first four days following a recent delivery?
back: The discharge is blood-stained (Lochia Rubra). It is the primary vaginal discharge occurring immediately after birth.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Lochia] discharge blood stained for first four days

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the appearance and duration of Lochia from the fourth to the tenth day post-delivery.
back: - Days 4–10: Becomes yellowish-white (Lochia Serosa). - By Day 10: Becomes white and offensive (Lochia Alba).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): yellowish-white after four days, white and offensive until tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Where is the uterine fundus palpable immediately following a recent full-term delivery?
back: - Palpable as a hard globe. - Located approximately five inches above the pubic symphysis (pubis).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: According to forensic standards, when does the uterine fundus typically sink behind the pubis post-delivery?
back: The uterus undergoes involution and typically sinks behind the pubic symphysis by the tenth day.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What specific findings on the inner surface of the uterus during autopsy indicate a recent delivery?
back: The inner surface shows clear evidence of the detachment of the placenta (placental site).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How is the presence of the Corpus Luteum interpreted during an autopsy in suspected delivery cases?
back: - Persists up to 10 days in a non-pregnant state after formation. - Persists until the fifth gestational month in pregnancy.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): presence of corpus luteum in non pregnant state up-to ten days after its formation and if pregnancy up to the fifth gestational month.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What anatomical changes in the birth canal suggest recent delivery in a living subject?
back: Presence of injuries to the birth canal, specifically tears of the vagina and possible perineal trauma.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the abdominal wall findings in a living subject shortly after a recent delivery.
back: The abdominal wall appears characteristically lax due to the sudden reduction in uterine volume.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Signs of recent event are the at-abdomen is lax

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the forensic significance of uterine weight during a post-mortem examination?
back: Uterine weight is measured to assess the stage of pregnancy or the degree of involution post-delivery.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Weight of uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Why do signs of remote (old) delivery lose forensic importance over time?
back: Remote signs depend on duration and lose diagnostic value as recent signs modify or disappear entirely.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How are signs of delivery categorized in forensic medicine?
back: Signs are categorized as either Recent or Remote (Old), depending on the time elapsed since the delivery event.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Proof of delivery will depend upon signs of full term pregnancy modified by event of delivery whether recent or remote.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the regression of uterine height during the first 10 days post-delivery.
back:
- Immediately: Palpable as a hard globe approx. 5 inches above the pubis.
- By 10th Day: Sinks behind the pubic symphysis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis. It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What are the three chronological stages of Lochia discharge?
back:
1. First 4 days: Blood-stained.
2. Next 2-3 days: Serous.
3. By 10th day: White and offensive.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): This discharge is blood stained for first four days, serous for next two or three days and offensive and white in color by the tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
coreConcept: Signs of Recent Delivery in Living
front: Q: List the external physical signs of a recent delivery in a living subject.
back:
- Lax abdominal wall.
- Injuries to the birth canal (vaginal tears).
- Palpable uterine globe (up to 10 days).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): In recent event abdomen is lax, uterus is palpable as a hard globe... injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What internal uterine finding at autopsy confirms recent delivery?
back: The inner surface of the uterus shows clear signs of placental detachment at the previous placental site.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Inner surface of the uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta. Placental site on the wall of the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the significance of the Corpus Luteum at autopsy regarding delivery?
back: The presence of a corpus luteum in a non-pregnant state indicates delivery within the previous 10 days.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Additional finding during autopsy is presence of corpus luteum in non-pregnant state up-to ten days after its formation.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Why are 'Remote' signs of delivery less medico-legally definitive?
back: They lose importance as recent signs like lochia and fresh tears disappear or modify over time.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: A woman presents with offensive white vaginal discharge 10 days post-trauma. Diagnosis?
back: Lochia Alba, indicating delivery approximately 10 days prior.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): specific soiling discharge called lochia... offensive and white in color by the tenth day.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What occurs to the birth canal during recent delivery?
back: It sustains physical trauma, typically manifested as tears of the vagina.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Other findings include injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How is the uterus described immediately after a full-term delivery?
back: It is palpable through the lax abdomen as a hard globe.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis.

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Where is the uterus palpable immediately following a recent full-term delivery?
back: It is palpable as a hard globe approximately five inches above the symphysis pubis.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Uterus is palpable as a hard globe about five inches above pubis.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Describe the characteristic color changes of Lochia during the first ten days postpartum.
back: 1. First 4 days: Blood-stained (Lochia Rubra). 2. Till 10th day: Pinkish or brown (Lochia Serosa).
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [discharge called lochia. This discharge is blood stained for first four days, then pinkish or brown and by tenth day it becomes offensive and white in color]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: By which day postpartum does the uterus typically sink behind the symphysis pubis?
back: The uterus typically sinks behind the pubis about the tenth day after delivery.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [It sinks behind pubis about the tenth day.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What internal uterine findings on autopsy confirm a recent full-term delivery?
back: 1. Large, thick-walled uterus. 2. Inner surface showing detachment of membranes. 3. Placental site measuring 4x3 inches.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of membranes and placental site is about 4x3 inches in a full term uterus]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What is the status of the ovarian corpus luteum in a woman recently delivered?
back: The corpus luteum is present in a non-pregnant state up to ten days after its formation.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [corpus luteum in non pregnant state is present up-to ten days after its formation]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: List the external signs of a recent delivery involving the birth canal and abdomen.
back: 1. Lax, wrinkled abdominal skin. 2. Reddish/purple striae gravidarum. 3. Tears or lacerations in the vagina.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [At-abdomen is lax, skin is wrinkled and bears striae-gravidarum... injuries to birth canal in the form of tears of vagina]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: How do signs of remote delivery differ from recent delivery in the living?
back: Recent signs (like Lochia or fresh tears) disappear or are modified into older indicators like silvery-white striae albicans.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Signs of remote event depend upon time duration and loose importance due to modification/disappearance of signs of recent event.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What happens to the placental site dimensions following delivery on autopsy?
back: The site initially measures 4x3 inches and gradually decreases to about 1 inch in diameter.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [placental site is about 4x3 inches... placental site size in the uterus has a relation to stage of pregnancy.]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: What specific breast changes are documented as signs of pregnancy and recent delivery?
back: Primary indicators include the enlargement and prominence of Montgomery's tubercles in the breasts.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [Signs in breasts: Enlargement of Montgomery's tubercles]

category: Explain recent and old signs of delivery in living and dead
front: Q: Define the biochemical nature of the vaginal discharge 'Lochia' after the 10th day.
back: After the tenth day, the discharge becomes white in color (Lochia Alba) and offensive in odor.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): [white in color by tenth day. Additional finding, during autopsy is presence of corpus luteum]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Define 'Killing of Fetus' according to the provided forensic text.
back:
- It is defined as the evacuation of a pregnant uterus.
- It may occur accidentally (spontaneous), therapeutically, or by criminal means.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Killing of fetus is evacuation of pregnant uterus. It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: How is abortion classified based on the legality and justification of the act?
back:
- Spontaneous: Accidental termination.
- Therapeutic: Induced in good faith to save the mother's life.
- Criminal: Unlawful termination using violence, drugs, or instruments.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means. Therapeutic abortion... performed in good faith for the sole purpose of saving life of mother.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Contrast the focus of early versus modern medico-legal codes regarding criminal miscarriage.
back:
- Early codes: Regarded criminal miscarriage as one of the most heinous crimes.
- Modern codes: Attitude is changing; services are often viewed as an index of civilization in Western countries.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Criminal miscarriage had been regarded as one of the most heinous crime in the early medico-legal codes... The attitude of society towards therapeutic abortion is changing dramatically.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Identify the conditions required for a registered medical practitioner to legally terminate a pregnancy in good faith.
back:
- To save the life of the pregnant woman.
- To prevent grave permanent injury to her physical or mental health.
citation: Page 28 (Book Page): [a registered medical practitioner... is of the opinion formed in good faith that the termination is immediately necessary to save the life or (ii) Prevent grave permanent injury to the physical or mental health of the pregnant women.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify abortifacient drugs that act directly on the uterus.
back:
- Ecbolics: Ergot, Quinine, Pituitary extract, Gossypicum.
- Emmenagogues: Synthetic estrogens, Borax, Oil of Savin.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Acting directly on the uterus: Ecbolics: Ergot, gossypicum, quinine, pitutiary extract. Emmenagogues: Synthetic estrogens, borax, oil of savin.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify abortifacient drugs that act indirectly on the uterus.
back:
- Emetics: Tartar emetic.
- Drastic Purgatives: Castor/Croton oils, Essential oils (Apiol, Juniper).
- Local Irritants: Salts of heavy metals (e.g., Oleate of Lead).
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Acting indirectly on the Uterus: Emetics: Tartar emetic. Drastic purgatives: Castor and croton oils, essential oils like apiol, juniper and turpentine. Local Irritants: Salts of heavy metals like oleate of lead.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify the three stages of criminal interference based on gestational duration.
back:
- Ovum Stage: First 14 days (uses direct violence).
- Embryo Stage: Up to 9th week (uses poisonous drugs).
- Fetal Stage: From 9th week till delivery (uses instrumentation).
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Stage: One (First 14 days) Methods: Violence (direct). Two (Ninth week) Methods: Poisonous drug. Three (Till delivery) Methods: Instrumentation.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: List the common instrumentation methods used in the third (fetal) stage of criminal abortion.
back:
- Probing instruments: Pencils, knitting needles, nails.
- Syringes: Higginson’s syringe loaded with disinfectants (Dettol) or soap water.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [In third fetal stage... All kinds of probing instruments such as pencils, knitting needles, nails are passed into the vagina... Higginson’s syringe loaded with disinfectant like dettol or even concentrated soap water.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify therapeutic abortion techniques based on the gestational period.
back:
- Up to 12 weeks: Dilatation and Curettage (D&C).
- After 12 weeks: Hysterotomy (Abdominal or Vaginal).
- Later stages: Vacuum suction or Amniocentesis.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Therapeutic techniques include: Dilatation and curettage (unto twelve weeks). Hysterotomy—(abdominal or vaginal) after twelve weeks. Amniocentesis—(abdominal or vaginal) later stages. Vacuum suction—(later stages).]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: According to Islamic principles in Pakistan, how does fetal gestation affect the classification of miscarriage?
back: - The offense becomes more serious when performed at a later stage of pregnancy after fetal organs or limbs have formed.
citation: Page 28 (Book Page): [law after its conformity with Islamic principles now takes into consideration two stages of fetal gestation making the offense of miscarriage more serious, when done at a later stage of pregnancy.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What is the medicolegal definition of abortion or miscarriage?
back: The evacuation of a pregnant uterus before full term gestation.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Killing of fetus is evacuation of pregnant uterus.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: How is abortion classified based on the nature of its occurrence?
back:
It is classified into three types:
* Spontaneous (Accidental)
* Therapeutic (Induced for medical grounds)
* Criminal (Induced by unauthorized means)
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: List the surgical techniques used in therapeutic abortion based on gestational age.
back:
* Dilatation and curettage (up to 12 weeks)
* Hysterotomy (after 12 weeks)
* Vacuum suction (later stages)
* Amniocentesis (later stages)
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Therapeutic techniques include: Dilatation and curettage (unto twelve weeks)... Hysterotomy... Amniocentesis... Vacuum suction.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: A pregnant woman dies instantly during a criminal abortion without hemorrhage. What is the likely mechanism?
back:
Vagal Shock:
* Triggered by cervical stimulation without anesthesia
* Causes sudden cardiac arrest
* Characterized by an absence of internal/external bleeding
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Death from vagal shock occurs in pregnant woman... without anesthesia... capable of producing Vagal inhibition and sudden arrest... almost instantaneous... no internal and external hemorrhage.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify abortifacient drugs used in criminal interference based on their site of action.
back:
* Indirect Action: Emetics, drastic purgatives, and local irritants
* Direct Action: Ecbolics (e.g., Ergot, Quinine) and Emmenagogues (e.g., synthetic estrogens)
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Abortifacient drugs list... Acting indirectly on the Uterus... Acting directly on the uterus...]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Match the stages of pregnancy to the primary methods used in criminal abortion.
back:
* Ovum Stage: Direct violence
* Embryo Stage: Poisonous drugs
* Fetal Stage: Instrumentation
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Stage 1 (Ovum): Violence. Stage 2 (Embryo): Poisonous drug. Stage 3 (Fetal): Instrumentation.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Distinguish between Isquat-i-Hamal and Isquat-i-Janin under the Qisas and Diyat Ordinance.
back:
* Isquat-i-Hamal: Causing miscarriage before fetal organs/limbs are formed
* Isquat-i-Janin: Causing miscarriage after fetal organs or limbs are formed
citation: Page 29 (Book Page): [Killing of child whose organs has not been formed... [Isquat-i-Hamal]. Killing of child whose limbs or organs have been formed... [Isquat-i-Janin].]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What is the primary differential diagnosis for rapid death following disinfectant injection via Higginson's syringe?
back:
Air Embolism:
* Air is pumped into the uterine cavity
* Membrane stripping exposes large vessels
* Negative venous pressure sucks air into the circulation
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): [Death from air embolism results from air being pumped into cavity of the womb, during an intrauterine injection. Stripping of membrane from uterine wall and detachment of the placenta expose large blood vessels.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What are the clinical consequences of delayed death following a criminal abortion?
back:
* Infection (e.g., septicemia from Clostridium welchii)
* Peritonitis or Pelvic cellulitis
* Renal failure
* Thrombo-phlebitis leading to pulmonary embolism
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): [Delayed death is due to infection such as renal failure... pelvic cellulitis or thrombo-phlebitis, which eventually cause pulmonary embolism and death.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Which specific internal autopsy findings confirm instrumental criminal interference in an abortion case?
back:
* Lacerations or perforations of the vagina, cervix, or uterus
* Presence of foreign fluids (soapy water or disinfectants) in the vagina
* Instrumental trauma marks on labia
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): [Vagina, cervix and uterus should be examined for evidence of instrumental trauma... injuries may be vagina, cervix or uterus... presence of foreign fluid is very common.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What is the medicolegal definition of an abortion?
back: It is the evacuation of the pregnant uterus. It can occur accidentally (spontaneous), be induced on medical grounds (therapeutic), or be performed by criminal means.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Killing of fetus is evacuation of pregnant uterus. It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: How is criminal abortion classified by method and gestational stage?
back:
• Ovum stage: Direct violence or hot baths.
• Embryo stage (to 9th week): Poisonous drugs.
• Fetal stage (to delivery): Instrumentation or probing.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Table 9.5] Stage One: Ovum... Violence; Stage Two: Embryo... Poisonous drug; Stage Three: Fetal... Instrumentation.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What distinguishes therapeutic from criminal abortion legally?
back: Therapeutic abortion is performed in good faith by authorized practitioners to save the mother's life or prevent grave permanent injury. Criminal abortion is illegal interference.
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): Therapeutic abortion... performed in good faith for the sole purpose of saving life of mother used to be considered as the only justified reason. Page 28 (Book Page): Prevent grave permanent injury to the physical or mental health of the pregnant women.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What is the likely mechanism of instant death during unanesthetized criminal instrumentation?
back: Vagal shock. Stimulus to the cervix precipitates vagal inhibition and sudden cardiac arrest. Autopsy shows no internal or external hemorrhage.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): Death from vagal shock occurs in pregnant woman, who is subjected to criminal interference withoutt anesthesia. Applied stimulus to neck of the womb... capable of precipitating Vagal inhibition and sudden arrest of heart.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify abortifacient drugs based on their directness of action.
back:
• Indirect: Emetics, drastic purgatives (Castor oil), and local irritants (Lead).
• Direct: Ecbolics (Ergot, Quinine) and amniogauges (Estrogens).
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Table 9.6] Abortifacient drugs list: Acting indirectly on the Uterus... Emetics... Drastic purgatives... Local Irritants... Acting directly on the uterus... Ecbolics... Amniogauges.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: List the common clinical techniques used for therapeutic abortion.
back:
• Dilatation and curettage (up to 12 weeks)
• Hysterotomy (after 12 weeks)
• Amniocentesis (later stages)
• Vacuum suction.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): Therapeutic techniques include: Dilatation and curettage... Hysterotomy... Amniocentesis... Vacuum suction.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of air embolism in criminal abortion.
back: Air is pumped into the womb during intrauterine injection. Placental detachment exposes large vessels; negative venous pressure sucks air into circulation, causing rapid death.
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): Death from air embolism results from air being pumped into cavity of the womb... Stripping of membrane from uterine wall and detachment of the placenta expose large blood vessels and negative pressure in veins may suck sufficient air... into the circulation.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Which organism causes post-abortion septicemia characterized by bronze skin?
back: Clostridium welchii. It becomes pathogenic in necrotic uterine tissues, leading to severe jaundice (bronze skin) and death within 12–48 hours.
citation: Page 98 (Book Page): In death from Septicemia, causative Organism generally is clostridium welchi... Skin of such a victim has a characteristic bronze color due to deep jaundice.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What are the primary causes of delayed death in criminal abortion?
back:
• Infection: Peritonitis or septicemia.
• Organ Failure: Renal failure.
• Thromboembolism: Pelvic cellulitis leading to pulmonary embolism.
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): Delayed death is due to infective complication like peritonitis or systemic such as renal failure... may develop late complications like pelvic cellulitis or thrombo-phlebitis, which eventually cause pulmonary embolism.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What local autopsy signs suggest a recent uterine evacuation?
back:
• Uterus palpable as a hard globe.
• Presence of lochia (vaginal discharge).
• Inner surface shows signs of placental detachment.
citation: Page 95 (Book Page): Uterus is palpable as a hard globe... specific vaginal discharge called lochia... Inner surface of uterus shows signs of detachment of placenta.

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Define abortion and name its three primary forensic classifications.
back:
Definition: The evacuation of the pregnant uterus (killing of the human fetus).
Classifications:
1. Spontaneous (accidental).
2. Therapeutic (medical grounds to save the mother).
3. Criminal (unlawful interference).
citation: Page 30 (Book Page): Killing of fetus is evacuation of pregnant uterus. It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means.

category: Define and classify abortions
coreConcept: Stages and Methods of Pregnancy Termination
front: Q: Classify the three stages of criminal abortion and list common therapeutic methods.
back:
Criminal Abortion Stages:
1. Ovum Stage (up to 14 days).
2. Embryo Stage (up to 9th week).
3. Fetal Stage (till delivery).
Therapeutic Methods: Dilatation and curettage, Hysterotomy, Amniocentesis, and Vacuum suction.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): Methods of criminal interference vary with duration of pregnancy dependent upon three stages of pregnancy... Stage 1 Ovum... Stage 2 Embryo... Stage 3 Fetal... Therapeutic techniques include: Dilatation and curettage... Hysterotomy... Amniocentesis... Vacuum suction.

category: Define and classify abortions
coreConcept: Forensic Definition and Basic Classification of Abortion
front: Q: How is 'killing of a human fetus' formally defined and primarily classified in forensic medicine?
back:
* Definition: Evacuation of a pregnant uterus.
* Classifications:
1. Accidental (Spontaneous)
2. Induced (Therapeutic on medical grounds)
3. Criminal (Unlawful interference)
citation: Page 27 (Book Page): [Killing of fetus is evacuation of pregnant uterus. It may occur accidentally as spontaneous, induced therapeutically on medical grounds or by criminal means.]

category: Define and classify abortions
coreConcept: Mechanism of Air Embolism in Abortion
front: Q: What is the pathophysiological mechanism of rapid death via air embolism in criminal abortion?
back:
* Stripping of membranes/placenta exposes large vessels.
* Negative venous pressure sucks air/fluid into circulation.
* Air travels via inferior vena cava to heart and pulmonary circulation.
citation: Page 97 (Book Page): [Death from air embolism results from air being pumped into cavity of the womb, durnng an intrauterine injection. Stripping of membrane from uterine wall and detachment of the placenta expose large blood vessels and negative pressure in veins may suck sufficient air and other fluid into the circulation.]

category: Define and classify abortions
coreConcept: Therapeutic vs. Criminal Abortion Legal Distinction
front: Q: Contrast the legal justification between therapeutic and criminal abortions.
back:
* Therapeutic: Performed in good faith by authorized practitioners solely to save the mother's life.
* Criminal: Unqualified/unauthorized interference intended to terminate pregnancy illegally.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [It is induced at various stages of pregnancy either by skilled and authorized medical practitioners, which is necessary to save life of mother or unqualified and unauthorized abortionist.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: A woman dies instantly during a non-anesthetized uterine interference with no signs of hemorrhage. Possible diagnosis?
back:
* Diagnosis: Vagal shock.
* Mechanism: Mechanical stimulus to the cervix (neck of womb) triggers vagal inhibition.
* Hallmark: Sudden cardiac arrest with zero internal or external bleeding.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Death from vagal shock occurs in a pregnant woman, who is subjected to manual interference withoutt anesthesia. Applied stimulus to neck of the womb is like stimulus to larynx or trachea. It is capable of producing vagal inhibition and sudden arrest of heart occurs almost instantaneous.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: How do 'Ecbolics' and 'Amniogauges' differ in their pharmacological action as abortifacients?
back:
* Ecbolics (e.g., Ergot, Quinine): Act directly on the uterine muscle to induce contraction.
* Amniogauges (e.g., Synthetic estrogens): Act as hormonal agents to initiate termination.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Abortifacient drugs list... Acting directly on the uterus: Ecbolics (Ergot, gossypicum, quinine, pitutiary extract); Amniogauges (Synthetic estrogens, borax, oil of savin)]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: List the four standard therapeutic techniques used for authorized medical termination of pregnancy.
back:
1. Dilatation and curettage (up to 12 weeks).
2. Hysterotomy (abdominal or vaginal; after 12 weeks).
3. Amniocentesis (later stages).
4. Vacuum suction (later stages).
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Therapeutic techniques include: Dilatation and curettage (unto twelve weeks); Hysterotomy—(abdominal or vaginal) after twelve weeks; Amniocentesis—(abdominal or vaginal) later stages; Vacuum suction—(later stages)]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Classify the stages of criminal termination of pregnancy based on the duration of gestation.
back:
* Stage One (Ovum): First nine days; uses direct violence.
* Stage Two (Embryo): Up to ninth week; uses poisonous drugs.
* Stage Three (Fetus): From ninth week till delivery; uses instrumentation.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Table 9.5: Stage of criminal termination of pregnancy: Stage One (Ovum) duration First nine days; Stage Two (Embryo) Ninth week; Stage Three (Fetal) Till delivery.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Differentiate between the causes of 'Rapid' and 'Delayed' maternal death in criminal abortion cases.
back:
* Rapid: Vagal shock, air embolism, or acute hemorrhage.
* Delayed: Sepsis (septicemia), peritonitis, renal failure, or pelvic cellulitis.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page)-97: [Death of Pregnant woman due to criminal interference is either rapid or delayed death. Rapid death gets precipitated because of Vagal Shock, air embolism or quick and massive hemorrhage. Delayed death is due to sepsis such as renal failure.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: Describe the uterine-vagal reflex loop that leads to sudden cardiac inhibition.
back: Stimulus to the cervix acts similarly to laryngeal stimulation, activating the vagus nerve. This leads to profound parasympathetic inhibition, causing immediate cardiac arrest.
citation: Page 96 (Book Page): [Applied stimulus to neck of the womb is like stimulus to larynx or trachea. It is capable of producing vagal inhibition and sudden arrest of heart occurs almost instantaneous.]

category: Define and classify abortions
front: Q: What is the primary causative organism and skin clinical hallmark in post-abortion septicemia?
back:
* Organism: Clostridium welchii.
* Hallmark: 'Bronze' skin color due to deep yellowish jaundice and necrotic tissue toxemia.
citation: Page 98 (Book Page): [In death from Septicemia, causative organism generally is clostridium welchii... Skin of such a victim has a characteristic bronze color due to deep jaundice yellowish.]

category: Describe their medico legal importance
coreConcept: Definition and Importance of Forensic Medicine
front: Q: What is the primary medico-legal objective of forensic medicine?
back: The application of medical knowledge to legal purposes for furthering justice. It provides unique public service through exclusive forensic certification for the administration of justice.
citation: Page 5 (Book Page): [Dealing with application of principles of medical knowledge to purposes of law and furthering of justice... Its importance is due to its unique public service necessity... acknowledged by law in connection with administration of justice.]

category: Describe their medico legal importance
front: Q: What is the medico-legal significance of finding a 'vital reaction' in a wound?
back: It confirms that the injury was sustained ante-mortem (during life). It is used to differentiate true injuries from post-mortem artifacts or scavenging marks.
citation: Page 55 (Book Page): [Post-mortem abrasion may be confused with ante-mortem abrasion especially when on Vital region like neck... Ante-mortem abrasion shows vital reaction.]

category: Describe their medico legal importance
front: Q: Describe the specific medico-legal importance of Cadaveric Spasm.
back: It indicates the last voluntary act of the victim at the moment of death. It is used to establish the manner of death, such as clutching a weapon in suicide.
citation: Page 134 (Book Page): [Its recognition and differentiation from rigor mortis is of immense importance... It indicates the last action before death... establishment of the manner of death.]
