category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: Forensic Specimen List for Sexual Assault
front: Q: What primary biological specimens are collected from a sexual assault victim for forensic analysis?
back:
• Stained clothing
• Swabs (vaginal, anal, and body stains)
• Loose hair and nail scrapings
• Urine (for drugs/venereal disease)
• Control specimens (blood, saliva, and plucked hair)
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Table 9.11: Comprehensive list of specimens: 1. Clothes entire lot (bearing stains and soiling) 2. Loose and matted hair 3. Swabs... 4. Scraping from undersurface of the nails... 5. Urine... 6. Control specimen]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: Preservation of Trace Evidence during Undressing
front: Q: How should a sexual assault victim be undressed to prevent the loss of trace evidence?
back:
• Victim must stand on a plain white sheet/cloth.
• Undressing should be performed unaided.
• All materials dropped during undressing must be collected and labeled.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Undressing should be done unaided by the examinee herself while standing on the sheet to avoid loss of trace evidence, Any items or material dropped during undressing should be collected]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What is the protocol for preserving wet blood or seminal stains on a victim's clothing?
back:
• Stains must be air-dried (not heat-dried).
• Encircle the dried stains with a permanent marker.
• Pack clothes in individual paper bags to prevent cross-contamination.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Wet stain is air dried and encircled with permanent marker before dispatch to the laboratory.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: List the four specific sites for vaginal swab collection during a medico-legal examination.
back:
1. Introitus/Perineum swabs.
2. Lower vaginal swabs.
3. High vaginal swabs.
4. Posterior fornix swabs (via speculum).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Table 9.11: Swabs... ii) From the vagina a) From introitus, perineum b) From lower vagina... c) From high vagina... iv) From the posterior fornix (with speculum into vagina on an applicator)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: Preparation and Packing of Seminal Smears
front: Q: How must seminal smear slides be packed to ensure they are fit for laboratory analysis?
back:
• Prepare air-dried smears.
• Pack two slides facing each other.
• Place matchsticks between slides at margins to prevent surface contact.
• Secure with adhesive tape.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Slides are also preserved by air-drying. The two are selected and packed having smeared surfaces facing each other with two matchsticks between them placed near the free margin of the slides.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Which specific specimens are collected from a male suspect to link him to the crime?
back:
• Swabs from the external urethral opening, glens penis, and penile shaft.
• Stained clothing (specifically the shalwar/trousers fly).
• Control specimens (blood, hair, and saliva).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [essential specimens from the assailant, besides those from other parts of the body, are swabs from external urethral opening, glens penis, rim of the glens and penile shaft... Fly of the trousers is usually stained with semen.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What control specimens are mandatory for comparison in sexual assault investigations?
back:
• Blood (for blood grouping).
• Plucked hair with roots intact (head and pubic hair).
• Saliva (for secretor status).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [6. Control specimen i) Blood... ii) Plucked hair (two each) a) Head hair b) Pubic hair iii) Saliva]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What details must be included on the label of every specimen container for the Chemical Examiner?
back:
• Date and place of collection.
• Name and source of specimen.
• Type of examination required.
• Signature/Designation of the collecting officer.
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Every container should bear a label with the following entries: Date and place of collection, Name of the specimen, From whom and from where collected, Type of examination required, Name and designation of person who collected specimen]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: How is the dispatch of specimens to the chemical examiner secured legally?
back:
• Containers must be sealed with a distinctive wax seal.
• A schedule of identity numbers for each specimen must be enclosed.
• Specimens must be transported via authorized police officials.
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Each specimen should be identified with an identity number and schedule showing identity numbers allotted to each specimen should be enclosed... Transportation of specimens to the laboratory should be done through the police official]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: In cases of suspected sodomy, what specific anal specimens are required?
back:
• Perianal swabs.
• Anal margin swabs.
• Lower rectal swabs (to detect internal spermatozoa).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [in case of sodomy, specimens from the victim are... perianal, anal and lower rectal swabs.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: Mandatory Control Specimens in Sexual Assault
front: Q: List the mandatory control specimens that must be collected from a sexual assault examinee.
back:
1. Blood.
2. Plucked head and pubic hair (with roots intact).
3. Saliva.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [6. Control specimen i) Blood ii) Plucked hair (two each) a) Head hair b) Pubic hair iii) Saliva]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Outline the specific preservation procedure for seminal swabs and slides collected from a victim.
back:
• Swabs: Air-dry thoroughly and place in separate, labeled test tubes.
• Slides: Smear once, air-dry, and pack with matchsticks between smeared surfaces to prevent contact.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Two are preserved by air-drying and placed in separate test tubes... Slides are also preserved by air-drying... packed having smeared surfaces facing each other with two matchsticks between them]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Contrast the collection techniques for dried seminal stains on skin versus internal vaginal semen.
back:
• External/Skin: Scrape with a dry scalpel or use a saline-moistened cotton swab.
• Internal/Vaginal: Use a sterile speculum to collect swabs from the introitus, lower vagina, and high vagina/fornix.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [From vaginal or anal canal... material is received on a cotton swab... with the help of a... speculum... When present on clothes, body... either be scraped with a dry scalpel or... moistened with saline]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: A victim presents with bite marks and scratches. Which specific specimens must be dispatched to identify the assailant?
back:
• Scraped nail deposits (contains suspect epithelium).
• Swabs from salivary stains on bite marks.
• Loose or matted hair found on the body.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Scraping from undersurface of the nails (epithelium of the assailant in non -consenting victims)... Salivary stains from the bite marks... Loose and matted hair]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define the legal term 'mens-rea' regarding an assailant's psycho-pathology.
back: Connotes evil or criminal intent; a prerequisite to guilt and a condition precedent to liability.
citation: Page 15 (Book Page): [Latin phrase mens-rea connotes evil or criminal intent, which is pre-requisite to guilt and thus a condition precedent to liability of the crime]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What three criteria establish insanity under the McNaughton’s Rules?
back:
1. Defect of reason from disease of mind.
2. Unknown nature/quality of action.
3. Unknown that action was wrong.
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [Defect of reason was due to disease of mind; He did not know nature and quality of his action; be did not know was doing wrong]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: How does the Durham Rule differ from McNaughton’s Rules regarding assailant responsibility?
back: McNaughton focuses on moral judgment capacity; Durham is based strictly on medical concepts (act is a product of mental disease).
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [In contrast to the McNaughton’s Rules, which takes into account the defendant's capacity to make moral judgment, the Durham Rule is based on purely medical concepts.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: An assailant knows their act is illegal but claims an uncontrollable urge. Name the applicable rule.
back: Irresistible Impulse (or 'Policeman at the shoulder' test); implies the defendant would have acted even with an officer present.
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [Irresistible Impulse also known as ‘Policeman at the shoulder’ meaning that the defendant, by reasons of disease of mind, would have acted as he did even had a policeman been standing at his side.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define the psychopathology of 'Sadism' in a sexual assailant.
back: Deriving sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty toward a partner of the opposite sex.
citation: Page 34 (Book Page): [Sadism: Sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty to partner of opposite sex]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What are the three primary exceptions that negate criminal responsibility?
back:
1. Immaturity (under age ten).
2. Insanity.
3. Involuntary intoxication.
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [Exception negates criminal responsibility and is also three. They are immaturity, insanity or intoxication at the time of commission of crime.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define 'Diminished responsibility' as it relates to an assailant's legal outcome.
back: The defendant is not completely absolved, but the severity of their sentence is mitigated or reduced.
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [Diminished responsibility is applicable to defendant who is not absolved completely, but the severity of his sentence gets mitigated or reduced.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Differentiate between the psychopathology of a 'Transvestite' and a 'Transsexual'.
back: Transvestite: Compulsion to cross-dress for gratification. Transsexual: Wish to identify as/adopt the opposite anatomical sex completely.
citation: Page 54 (Book Page): [Transvestite is the one who is obsessed with the clothing of the opposite sex having compulsion to cross- dress. Transsexual has a dominant wish to identify with the opposite sex as completely as possible discarding forever his or her own anatomical sex]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: When is an assailant declared 'Unfit to Plead' in a court of law?
back: When the defendant was sane during the crime but subsequently became insane and unable to defend themselves.
citation: Page 14 (Book Page): [Unfit to plead, applicable when the defendant was sane at the time of commission of crime but has subsequently become insane and thus not capable of defending himself.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: In substantive criminal law, what does 'actus-reus' represent?
back: Represents the physical evil action or the execution of the criminal intention.
citation: Page 15 (Book Page): [Latin phrase actus-reus represents evil action. In absence of either of the two, the crime cannot be considered as committed.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: What are the two essential prerequisites before initiating a medico-legal examination in sexual offences?
back:
1. Expressed written consent from the examinee.
2. Verification of personal identity through bio-data and identification marks.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Forensic medical examination of both the victim and offender should be done immediately after taking proper written Consent from them. It is undertaken in proper medical surrounding by qualified medical practitioner and should be thorough, complete in all respects... Verification of examinee’s personal identity essential]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Describe the anatomical changes seen in the anal canal in cases of habitual sodomy.
back: The anal canal becomes lax and patulous, with loss of normal corrugator cutis ani folds (rugosities) and a smooth mucosal surface.
citation: Page 104 (Book Page): [A habitual’s canal is lax, with absence of normal anal folds and margins appear smooth. Anal canal is patulous and may also be infected.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Contrast the primary physical positions used for vaginal versus anal medico-legal examinations.
back:
1. Vaginal: Lithotomy position.
2. Anal: Knee-elbow position.
Both require adequate illumination and use of specula/proctoscopes.
citation: Page 102 (Book Page)/103: [Vaginal examination requires proper positioning of the female victim. Place the victim in the lithotomy position... Anal examination is performed in knee-elbow position; its sub-stages are similar to those of vaginal examination.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Why is the hymen often spared in prepubescent victims of sexual assault?
back: In children, the hymen is situated high up in the vaginal canal; injuries typically present as posterior vaginal wall lacerations or perineal tears.
citation: Page 102 (Book Page): [Hymen in children is situated high up in the vaginal canal and therefore usually gets speared and shows no rupture, but instead vaginal canal is torn posteriorly Proportionate to disproportion.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: How must wet biological stains on clothing be processed before dispatch to the laboratory?
back: Stains must be air-dried on hangers (never heat-dried), encircled with a permanent marker, and signed by the examiner.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Wet stain is air dried and encircled with permanent marker before dispatch to the laboratory.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: List the four mandatory stages for the clinical scrutiny of the vaginal or anal canal.
back:
1. Inspection
2. Bilateral traction
3. Digital manipulation
4. Instrumental (speculum/proctoscope) scrutiny
citation: Page 111 (Book Page): [There are four sub-stages: Inspection, Bilateral traction, Digital manipulation, Instrumental scrutiny]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Explain the diagnostic purpose of using bilateral traction during an anal examination.
back: It stretches the anal sphincter to expose the skin-mucosal junction and reveal fissures or triangular tears with the base toward the lumen.
citation: Page 103 (Book Page): [Bilateral traction of anal sphincter with the help of thumbs of both hands locates any anal tear or fissure. Anal tear becomes visible as triangular damage having base towards the lumen of the canal.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: How is an ante-mortem anal fissure differentiated from post-mortem scavenging damage?
back: Ante-mortem fissures show vital reactions (bruising/hyperemia), while scavenging produces dry, parchment-like edges often showing peripheral teeth marks.
citation: Page 140 (Book Page): [Examination of such injuries (scavenging), when made through magnifying lens shows no vital reaction and teeth marks become clearly visible at the periphery... Denuded area dries rapidly and presents a brown parchment like appearance]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: What biochemical enzyme is specific to prostatic secretions and serves as the primary screening marker for semen?
back: Acid Phosphatase. Semen contains high concentrations (4000–8000 IU), far exceeding other body fluids.
citation: Page 102 (Book Page): [Fluid portion has a high quantity of prostatic secretion, which is rich, both in acid phosphatase enzyme having 4000 to 8000 units /U- in contrast to other body fluids]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: What specific trace evidence should be collected from under the fingernails of a non-consenting victim?
back: Skin epithelium or blood from the assailant, collected using scrapings with a dry scalpel or pointed scissors.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Scraping from undersurface of the nails (epithelium of the assailant in non -consenting victims)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What primary specimens must be collected from a sexual assault victim for chemical analysis?
back:
* Entire lot of clothing (bearing stains/soiling)
* Loose and matted hair
* Swabs (vaginal, anal, salivary)
* Nail scrapings
* Urine and control blood samples
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Comprehensive list of specimens: 1. Clothes entire lot... 2. Loose and matted hair 3. Swabs... 4. Scraping from undersurface of the nails... 5. Urine... 6. Control specimen (Blood, Plucked hair, Saliva)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What are the four specific vaginal sites required for swab collection in sexual assault?
back:
1. Introitus/Perineum
2. Lower vagina (above hymeneal boundary)
3. High vagina
4. Posterior fornix (via speculum)
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [ii) From the vagina a) From introitus, perineum b) From lower vagina... c) From high vagina iv) From the posterior fornix (with speculum into vagina on an applicator)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: How are swabs and slides from a sexual assault examination preserved before dispatch?
back:
* Swabs: Air-dried and placed in separate test tubes
* Slides: Prepared with thin smears and air-dried
* Avoid moist storage to prevent bacterial decomposition
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Two are preserved by air-drying and placed in separate test tubes for dispatch to the laboratory. The third swab, while still wet, is used to prepare two slides... Slides are also preserved by air-drying.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Describe the proper packing technique for dispatching two glass slides containing smears.
back:
* Place smeared surfaces facing each other
* Insert matchsticks between slides at margins to prevent contact
* Wrap with adhesive tape and label
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Packed having smeared surfaces facing each other with two matchsticks between them placed near the free margin of the slides. The slides should be wrapped with adhesive tape to avoid displacement and loss of specimen.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: In a non-consenting victim, what is the significance of collecting nail scrapings?
back: To identify the suspect's epithelium or blood deposited during resistance. Scrapings are collected from the undersurface into a clean test tube.
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Scraping from undersurface of the nails (epithelium of the assailant in non-consenting victims)... preserved with the help of sharp pointed scissors or a scalpel and placed directly in a test tube.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What specimens should be collected specifically from the suspect in a sexual assault case?
back:
* Swabs: External urethral opening, glans penis, and penile shaft
* Clothes: Specifically the trouser fly/shalwar for seminal stains
* Control samples: Blood, hair, and saliva
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Essential specimens from the assailant... are swabs from external urethral opening, glans penis, rim of the glans and penile shaft. Clothes... seminal stains, which are commonly found on the trouser or shalwar... Fly of the trousers is usually stained with semen.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: How should dried seminal stains on non-absorbent surfaces be collected for the chemical examiner?
back:
* Scrape with a dry scalpel onto glazed paper
* Alternatively, moisten area with saline and collect on a cotton swab
citation: Page 161 (Book Page): [Should either be scraped with a dry scalpel and collected in glazed paper and then passed into a special container... Alternately this area may be moistened with saline and the material taken on a cotton swab.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What mandatory information must be included on each specimen label during dispatch?
back:
* Date and place of collection
* Specimen name and source
* Type of examination required
* Medical examiner's name and designation
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Every container should bear a label with the following entries: i. Date and place of collection ii. Name of the specimen iii. From whom and from where collected iv. Type of examination required v. Name and designation of person who collected specimen]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What procedure ensures the integrity of specimens during transit to the laboratory?
back:
* Maintain a "Chain of Custody"
* Seal containers with distinctive wax devices
* Transport via an authorized police official with a signed receipt
citation: Page 107 (Book Page)/111: [Maintains chain of custody of forensic samples... Sealing of each container is under taken by... distinctive device in such a manner that any tampering would be immediately become obvious... handed over only after obtaining a receipt.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Why is a urine specimen collected from a sexual assault victim for the chemical examiner?
back: To screen for possible drugs used for incapacitation (poisoning) and to detect venereal diseases (STIs).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page)/160: [Urine for screening of drugs and venereal disease... is usually taken for estimation of alcohol and other poisons... to detect spermatozoa and gonococci.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: List of Specimens for Sexual Assault
front: Q: What primary biological specimens are collected from a sexual assault victim for the chemical examiner?
back:
• Entire lot of clothes
• Swabs (vaginal, anal, body stains)
• Smear slides
• Loose/matted hair
• Nail scrapings
• Control samples (blood, saliva, plucked hair).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [1. Clothes entire lot (bearing stains and soiling) 2. Loose and matted hair 3. Swabs... 4. Scraping from undersurface of the nails... 6. Control specimen]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Describe the mechanism of collecting trace evidence during the undressing phase of the forensic examination.
back: The examinee must stand on a large, clean white sheet while undressing unaided. This captures any items (hair, fibers, debris) dropped during the process for laboratory analysis.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Examination of clothes should be done making the examinee stand on plain white cloth free from any contamination. Undressing should be done unaided by the examinee herself while standing on the sheet to avoid loss of trace evidence.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Compare the preservation method for wet seminal stains on clothes versus vaginal swabs.
back: Both must be air-dried at room temperature before dispatch. Wet stains are never packed directly to prevent bacterial destruction of the DNA/enzymes.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Wet stain is air dried and encircled with permanent marker before dispatch to the laboratory.] Page 105 (Book Page): [Two are preserved by air-drying and placed in separate test tubes for dispatch.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
coreConcept: Anatomical Swab Sites in Sexual Assault
front: Q: A victim presents 48 hours post-assault; what specific swab sites are mandatory for genital examination?
back:
• Introitus and perineum
• Lower vagina (above hymeneal boundary)
• High vagina/Posterior fornix (collected via speculum).
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [ii) From the vagina a) From introitus, perineum b) From lower vagina... c) From high vagina... iv) From the posterior fornix (with speculum into vagina on an applicator)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What specific preservative is used for viscera and tissue samples in toxicology cases?
back: Super saturated sodium chloride (saline) is the standard preservative. Saturated saline or rectified spirit are utilized to maintain integrity against decomposition.
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Saturated sodium chloride solution... is an alternate choice... Rectified spirit is a good and effective preservative for all types of viscera collected for chemical analysis.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: What are the specific requirements for the specimen containers used in sexual assault dispatch?
back:
• Impervious glass or plastic
• Chemically clean/dry
• Wide-mouthed
• Fitted with secure screw-type stoppers.
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Container of specimen should be impervious, clean and free from contamination... Mouth of container should be appropriately wide... Stopper of container should be screw-type.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: How is a smear slide correctly prepared and packed for the chemical examiner?
back: The swab is rubbed once on the slide. After air-drying, two slides are placed with smeared faces inward, separated by matchsticks to prevent surface contact, then wrapped in adhesive tape.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [The slides are also preserved by air-drying. The two are selected and packed having smeared surfaces facing each other with two matchsticks between them placed near the free margin.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Contrast the collection of nail scrapings for the assailant’s DNA versus victim’s debris.
back: Nail scrapings are taken from the undersurface of free ends using a clean scalpel or pointed scissors to recover epithelial cells or blood trapped during resistance.
citation: Page 105 (Book Page): [Scraping from undersurface of the nails (epithelium of the assailant in non-consenting victims)]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Why is 100cc of blood required specifically from the right heart in forensic poisoning cases?
back: It is the specimen of choice for detecting alcohol and carbon monoxide, as central blood better represents the systemic poison concentration before post-mortem distribution.
citation: Page 160 (Book Page): [c) 100 cc in poisoning case from right heart is specimen of choice in carbon monoxide and alcohol poisoning.]

category: Outline collection, preservation and dispatch of specimens in cases of sexual assaults to chemical examiner
front: Q: Outline the physical sealing requirements for specimen boxes before police dispatch.
back: Containers are wrapped in heavy paper, tied with cotton cord, and sealed with wax using a distinctive device to ensure immediate detection of tampering.
citation: Page 159 (Book Page): [Sealing of each container is under taken by wrapping it with heavy paper, tie its top and bottom with a cotton cord, seal applied over the knot with sealing wax and mark wax seal with some distinctive device.]

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
coreConcept: Signs of Resistance in Sexual Assault
front: Q: Which extragenital sites of bruising typically indicate resistance in a sexual assault victim?
back:
• Medial thighs and knees (forced separation)
• Forearms and arms (gripping)
• Cheeks and breasts (often bite marks)
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): Bruises, in female victim, are on her forearms and arms mostly due to gripping... medial sides of knees and thighs due to an attempt to separate them and on cheek and breast caused by bites.

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Differentiate between hymenal tears caused by digital penetration versus sexual intercourse.
back:
• Digital: Usually incomplete and situated at anterior or posterior sites.
• Intercourse: Usually complete and radiating laterally.
citation: Page 102 (Book Page): Digital tears are incomplete and are generally situated either at anterior or posterior sites... whereas tears due to sexual intercourse are complete and radiate laterally.

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: Describe the characteristic appearance of an acute anal tear in an unnatural sexual offense.
back: It presents as a triangular laceration with the base directed towards the anal lumen, potentially involving the sphincter and mucosa.
citation: Page 103 (Book Page): Anal tear or fissure... appearing as triangular damage having base towards the lumen of the canal... Anal tears or fissure may also extend into the anal mucosa.

category: Describe the medico-legal examination in unnatural sexual offence
front: Q: How is the presence of vaginal epithelium demonstrated on the suspect's penis?
back: By painting the glans with dilute iodine solution; the vaginal epithelial cells will stain a characteristic deep brown.
citation: Page 104 (Book Page): Vaginal epithelium may stick on the glans penis and can easily be detected by painting it with dilute iodine solution. Vaginal epithelium stains deep brown.

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What are the three specific exceptions that negate the criminal responsibility of an assailant?
back:
1. Immaturity (child under age ten).
2. Insanity (adult with mental illness).
3. Involuntary Intoxication (intake without knowledge or will).
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Exception negates criminal responsibility of the accused and is also three. They are immaturity, insanity or intoxication at the time of commission of crime. A child under the age of ten, an adult suffering from mental illness and an intoxicated individual are not considered competent to understand the nature and consequences of their action thus are not guilty.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Describe the three components of the McNaughton’s Rules for resolving the plea of insanity.
back:
1. Defect of reason due to disease of mind.
2. Assailant did not know the nature and quality of the action.
3. Assailant did not know the act was wrong.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [McNaughton’s Rules... Defect of reason was due to disease of mind; Due to disease of mind, He did not know nature and quality of his action; If he did know nature and quality of his action, he did not know, was doing wrong.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Contrast the McNaughton’s Rules with the Durham Rule in evaluating an assailant's mental state.
back: McNaughton's relies on the assailant's capacity for moral judgment (right vs wrong), while the Durham Rule is based strictly on medical concepts of mental disease.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [In contrast to the McNaughton’s Rules, which takes into account the defendant's capacity to make moral judgment, the Durham Rule is based on purely medical concepts.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Clinical Scenario: An assailant was sane during the crime but becomes insane before trial. Identify the appropriate verdict.
back: Unfit to Plead. The court proceedings are suspended until the defendant's sanity is restored sufficiently to defend themselves.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Unfit to plead, applicable when the defendant was sane at the time of commission of crime but has subsequently become insane and thus not capable of defending himself. The court proceeding gets suspended till such time that defendant's sanity is restored.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What is the defining characteristic of the 'Irresistible Impulse' or 'Policeman at the shoulder' test?
back: The defendant would have committed the act even if a policeman had been standing at their side due to a disease of the mind.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Americans have supplemented the McNaughton’s Rules by “Irresistible Impulse” also known as ‘Policeman at the shoulder’ meaning that the defendant, by reasons of disease of mind, would have acted as he did even had a policeman been standing at his side.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define the verdict of 'Diminished Responsibility' for an accused assailant.
back: The assailant is not completely absolved of guilt, but the severity of their sentence is mitigated or reduced due to their mental state.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Diminished responsibility is applicable to defendant who is not absolved completely, but the severity of his sentence gets mitigated or reduced.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What two legal elements are essential to prove a crime has been committed by an assailant?
back:
1. Mens-rea: The evil or criminal intent (mental element).
2. Actus-reus: The evil action (physical execution). Both must be present.
citation: Page 12 (Book Page): [Latin phrase mens-rea connotes evil or criminal intent... Latin phrase actus-reus represents evil action. In absence of either of the two, the crime cannot be considered as committed.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Differential Case: Distinguish between Sadism and Masochism in the context of sexual psychopathology.
back: Sadism involves sexual pleasure derived from acts of cruelty toward a partner. Masochism involves sexual pleasure derived from pain or injury inflicted by the partner.
citation: Page 31 (Book Page): [Sadism: Sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty to partner of opposite sex; Masochism: Sexual pleasure from pain/injury inflicted by partner of the opposite sex.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Describe the methodology and primary sources utilized for conducting a 'Psychological Autopsy'.
back: A specialized exercise to determine the deceased's mental status. Information is collected from family, friends, teachers, professional colleagues, and their physician.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Psychological autopsy is special exercise in cases of alleged suicide. It is to know deceased's mental status at the time of his death... Sources for collection of this information are family members, teachers, friends, professional colleagues and his physician.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What is the legal definition of an 'Assault' regarding the assailant's gestures?
back: Any gesture or preparation intended to cause the victim to apprehend that criminal force is about to be used against them.
citation: Page 12 (Book Page): [Assault: Whoever makes any gesture or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Why is mental status evaluation prioritized over physical trauma in sexual assault cases?
back: Assaults typically cause more significant psychological damage than physical injury; victims are often emotionally tense, withdrawn, or suicidal.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): Evaluation of mental status is both essential and important as such assaults cause more psychological damage than physical trauma.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the underlying mechanism of psychogenic amnesia in forensic victims?
back: It occurs due to extreme psychological stress rather than brain damage, resulting specifically in interference with the process of recall.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): Psychogenic amnesia, on the other hand, occurs in situations of psychological stress causing interference in the process of recall.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Define the psychopathological state of a Transsexual individual during assessment.
back: The victim has a dominant wish to identify with the opposite sex and permanently discard their own anatomical sex.
citation: Page 51 (Book Page): Transsexual has a dominant wish to identify with the opposite sex as completely as possible discarding forever his or her own anatomical sex.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Interpret the clinical presentation of a zina-bil-jabr victim who refuses to narrate the incident.
back: The victim is likely depressed, withdrawn, and emotionally tense; refusal occurs because the recall of the event is psychologically painful.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): Female victim of zina-bil-jabr is emotionally very tense, withdrawn, depressed and entertains suicidal ideas. She may become reluctant to narrate the incidence, as recall is painful.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the primary forensic objective of performing a Psychological Autopsy?
back: To determine the deceased's mental status, personality traits, and habits at the time of death, especially in cases of alleged suicide.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): Psychological autopsy is special exercise in cases of alleged suicide. It is to know deceased’s mental status at the time of his death.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What broad diagnosis covers hysteria or anxiety following a traumatic head injury?
back: Post-traumatic neurosis, which is now more commonly interpreted under the broader diagnosis of Post-Traumatic Stress Syndrome (PTSS).
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): Post-traumatic neurosis and some other states like hysteria, anxiety and broader diagnosis of post-traumatic stress syndrome.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: List the four key parameters for assessing a victim's mental state during forensic certification.
back:
1. Variation of mood
2. Concentration of mind
3. Orientation to space and time
4. Psychomotor response
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): It is assessed by noticing variation of mood, concentration of mind, orientation about space and time, victim's behavior and psychomotor response.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Contrast the psychopathology of a Transvestite victim with a Transsexual victim.
back: Transvestite: Compulsion to cross-dress in opposite-sex clothing. Transsexual: Desire to completely change anatomical sex identity.
citation: Page 51 (Book Page): Transvestite is the one who is obsessed with the clothing of the opposite sex... Transsexual has a dominant wish to identify with the opposite sex as completely as possible.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How does the psychological state of 'agony' during death affect postmortem blood findings?
back: Sudden/painful death creates emotional tension, stimulating vascular endothelium to secrete fibrinolysin, which keeps blood in a fluid state.
citation: Page 134 (Book Page): It stimulated production of fibrinolysin by vascular endothelium into blood circulation, which dissolved the already formed clot. There was no anxiety in the first group.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What defines the psychopathological condition of 'Sadism' in sexual indulgence?
back: Deriving acute psychological gratification or sexual pleasure specifically from acts of cruelty toward a partner of the opposite sex.
citation: Page 34 (Book Page): Sadism: Sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty to partner of opposite sex.

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
coreConcept: Psychological State of Sexual Assault Victims
front: Q: What common psychological symptoms are characteristic of a female victim of Zina-bil-jabr?
back:
• Emotionally tense and withdrawn.
• Depressed with potential suicidal ideation.
• Reluctance to narrate the incident due to painful recall and thought block.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Female victim of zina-bil-jabr ‘is emotionally very tense, withdrawn, depressed and entertains suicidal ideas. She may become reluctant to narrate the incidence, as recall is painful and requires, support and encouragement to overcome this feeling.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the underlying mechanism that distinguishes psychogenic amnesia from organic post-traumatic amnesia?
back:
• Organic: Neuronal disturbance via chemical, traumatic, or degenerative changes.
• Psychogenic: Psychological stress causing active interference in the process of memory recall.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Organic amnesia results from pathological changes in the brain and occurs due to disturbance of neurons... Psychogenic amnesia, on the other hand, occurs in situations of psychological stress causing interference in the process of recall.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Differentiate between Anterograde and Retrograde amnesia in the context of post-traumatic psycho-pathology.
back:
• Anterograde: Memory loss extending forwards from the moment of injury.
• Retrograde: Memory loss extending backwards from the moment consciousness is regained.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Post-traumatic amnesia is of two types: Antrograde amnesia extending forwards from the time of injury [and] Retrograde amnesia extending backwards from the time of regaining of consciousness.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Which specific data sets are required to interpret a victim's mental state via 'Psychological Autopsy'?
back:
• Deceased's background, habits, and personality traits.
• Quality of interpersonal relationships.
• Mental status at the immediate time of death.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Psychological autopsy... is to know deceased's mental status at the time of his death. ... data includes deceased's background, habit, personality trait and quality of relationship with others.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: In cases of sexual assault, does psychological damage or physical trauma take clinical precedence during victim evaluation?
back:
- Psychological damage is considered more essential and important than physical trauma.
- Assessment of mental status is a mandatory forensic requirement.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [evaluation of mental status is both essential and important as such assaults cause more psychological damage than physical trauma]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the underlying mechanism responsible for psychogenic amnesia in forensic victims of acute stress?
back:
- It is a functional interference in the process of recall.
- Termed as "forgetting," it is triggered by trauma rather than organic brain damage.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Psychogenic amnesia... occurs in situations of psychological stress causing interference in the process of recall. Strictly speaking, 'forgetting' is psychogenic amnesia]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How is the origin of organic amnesia differentiated from psychogenic amnesia in a forensic victim?
back:
- Organic: Pathological brain changes (chemical/trauma) impairing registration and retention.
- Psychogenic: Purely functional failure of recall due to psychological stress.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Organic amnesia results from pathological changes in the brain... It impairs both registration and retention. Psychogenic amnesia... [is] interference in the process of recall.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: A sexual assault victim appears withdrawn, silent, and suicidal. Which psychopathological presentation does this typically represent?
back:
- This characterizes the emotionally tense and depressed state common in Zina-bil-jabr victims.
- It often leads to reluctance in narrating the incidence.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Female victim of zina-bil-jabr is emotionally very tense, withdrawn, depressed and entertains suicidal ideas. She may become reluctant to narrate the incidence]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How does acute intoxication specifically manifest during the assessment of a victim’s mental status?
back:
- Presents as disorientation, semi-coma, or convulsive states.
- Causes retarded psychomotor responses and impaired concentration.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [intoxicated patient's are either unconscious, comatose or even in convulsive state also manifesting disorientation... psychomotor responses in such a case are retarded]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What clinical entities are grouped under the broader diagnosis of post-traumatic stress syndrome for victims?
back:
- Post-traumatic neurosis.
- Characterized by hysteria, anxiety, and depression following the traumatic event.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Post-traumatic neurosis consists of symptoms like hysteria, anxiety and depression... broader diagnosis of post-traumatic stress syndrome.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Define the psychopathological state "run amok" associated with chronic cannabis use in offenders or victims.
back:
- A state of moral degradation with an irresistible impulse to destroy.
- Characterized specifically by indiscriminate murdering of people.
citation: Page 185 (Book Page): [irresistible impulse to destroy life and property, which may lead to 'run amok'. It is a state... characterized by indiscriminate murdering.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Which specific sources provide the most reliable data for a psychological autopsy of a suspected suicide victim?
back:
- Family members, teachers, and friends.
- Professional colleagues and the victim's personal physician.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Sources for collection of this information are family members, teachers, friends, professional colleagues and his physician]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: In what order do memories typically return to a victim suffering from post-traumatic retrograde amnesia?
back:
- Memories recover in chronological order.
- Oldest memories return first; those nearest the injury are the last to recover.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Recall is in chronological order, these memories nearest to injury being the last to recover.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What specific psychomotor change is observed in victims finding it difficult to narrate a sexual assault?
back:
- Retarded psychomotor responses.
- Manifests as confusion and significant thought block.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Psychomotor responses in such a case are retarded with disturbance of concentration of mind. Victim may be confused showing thought block]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is a psychological autopsy and when is it primarily utilized in forensic practice?
back: It is a retrospective mental status evaluation used in alleged suicide cases to determine the deceased’s state of mind and personality traits at the time of death.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Psychological autopsy is special exercise in cases of alleged suicide. It is to know deceased's mental status at the time of his death.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How does Organic amnesia differ from Psychogenic amnesia regarding the recall process?
back: Organic amnesia results from physical brain damage impairing registration and retention. Psychogenic amnesia is 'forgetting' due to psychological stress, causing interference specifically in the process of recall.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Organic amnesia results from pathological changes in the brain... it impairs both registration and retention. Psychogenic amnesia, on the other hand, occurs in situations of psychological stress causing interference in the process of recall.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Distinguish between Anterograde and Retrograde amnesia following a head injury.
back: Anterograde amnesia extends forward from the time of injury. Retrograde amnesia extends backward from the moment consciousness is regained, covering events immediately preceding the trauma.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Antrograde amnesia extending forwards from the time of injury. Retrograde amnesia extending backwards from the time of regaining of consciousness.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: A sexual assault victim appears withdrawn, depressed, and displays retarded psychomotor responses. Interpret these findings.
back: These are psychopathological indicators of acute psychological damage following sexual violation (zina-bil-jabr). Victims often experience thought block, confusion, and suicidal ideation, which exceed physical trauma in gravity.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page)/110: [Female victim of zina-bil-jabr is emotionally very tense, withdrawn, depressed... psychomotor responses in such a case are retarded with disturbance of concentration of mind.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What constitutes the 'post-traumatic neurosis' syndrome following a head injury?
back: It is a psychological stress syndrome characterized by hysteria, anxiety, and depression. It occurs without demonstrable anatomical lesions and is influenced by social, psychological, and economical factors.
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Post-traumatic neurosis... including hysteria, anxiety and depression... broader diagnosis of post-traumatic stress syndrome.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: List the four key observations required for evaluating the mental state of a forensic examinee.
back:
1. Variation of mood. 
2. Concentration of mind. 
3. Orientation regarding space and time. 
4. Psychomotor responses and general behavior.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Mental state is important... assessed by noticing variation of mood, concentration of mind, orientation about space and time, victim's behavior and psychomotor response.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How does the offender's behavior before and after an incident help distinguish true amnesia from feigned?
back: Attempts to run or conceal the act suggest knowledge of the crime, indicating amnesia is likely feigned. True amnesia (e.g., in epilepsy) typically involves no attempt at concealment.
citation: Page 90 (Book Page): [Behavior of the victim before and after incidence is important evidence... An attempt by the offender to run or conceal the act suggests knowledge of what he has done.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Differentiate the psychological manifestations of Datura poisoning from acute schizophrenia.
back: Datura causes delirious states with fits of laughter, visual hallucinations, and purposeless movements (e.g., picking imaginary objects). It is distinguished by physical anticholinergic signs like dilated pupils and dry skin.
citation: Page 183 (Book Page): [He may suffer from fits of laughter with delusions and may perform purposeless movements... Differential diagnosis is from alcoholic delirium and acute schizophrenia.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Why must a forensic medical examiner prioritize the evaluation of mental status in non-fatal trauma cases?
back: Physical aggression often causes more profound psychological damage than physical trauma. Mental state assessment is essential to determine the true gravity of damage and resulting incapacitation.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [In these cases, evaluation of mental status is both essential and important as such assaults cause more psychological damage than physical trauma.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Which sources provide data for the compilation of a victim's psychological background in forensics?
back: Family members, teachers, friends, professional colleagues, and the victim’s personal physician are the primary sources for collecting data on habits and personality traits.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Sources for collection of this information are family members, teachers, friends, professional colleagues and his physician who is more knowledgeable.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the first legal prerequisite before conducting a forensic medical examination of a living victim?
back:
* Expressed written consent of the examinee.
* Essential to avoid legal liability or allegations of assault.
citation: Page 6 (Book Page): [Expressed written consent of examinee, a prerequisite]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Why is immediate examination at an authorized center preferred over referral to a distant facility?
back:
* Prevents loss of vital evidence during transit.
* Avoids cleansing of parts (sexual assault) or onset of injury repair/infection.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [Transportation outside to other medical facility is even inadvisable, because of chances for loss of vital evidence during transit, cleansing of parts especially in sexual assaults.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Contrast the initial gastric management of general poisoning versus corrosive acid ingestion.
back:
* General: Immediate gastric lavage using warm water/saline.
* Corrosive: Gastric lavage is strictly contraindicated due to perforation risk.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [It is done nearly in all cases of ingested poison except when contraindicated as in poisoning by corrosive.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Which procedural safeguards are mandatory when managing a female victim of sexual assault?
back:
* Presence of a female attendant during examination.
* Examinee must undress herself unaided to avoid assault allegations.
citation: Page 106 (Book Page): [Examination of female (sexual assault) undertaken in presence of a female attendant and un-dressing done by herself to avoid allegation of assault]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the primary physiological priority when managing a victim of acute hypnotic overdose?
back:
* Maintaining a clear airway.
* Prevents irreversible cerebral anoxia and subsequent hypoxia.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [Most important step is to keep the airway clear from the moment the patient is first seen until recovery... to ensure that patient has a clear airway.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Which vital signs must be documented during the initial physical status assessment of a trauma victim?
back:
* Body temperature.
* Blood pressure.
* Pulse and respiratory rates (with character).
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Cases of trauma needs recording of body temperature, blood pressure, pulse and respiratory rates with their character]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How should wet, blood-stained garments from a victim be managed to preserve forensic integrity?
back:
* Air-dry on hangers (do not apply heat).
* Encircle stains and sign with a permanent marker before laboratory dispatch.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Wet stain is air dried and encircled with permanent marker before dispatch to the laboratory.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: A victim presents with pinpoint pupils and slow respiration. What specific pharmacological reversal is indicated?
back:
* Naloxone (Pure narcotic antagonist).
* Dosage: 0.4-0.8 mg intravenously for adults.
citation: Page 169 (Book Page): [Naloxone is a pure narcotic antagonist and is the recommended drug of choice for reversal of overdose doses of narcotic analgesics... 0.4-0.8 mg/kg body weight in the adults]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Describe the initial clinical stabilization step for an organophosphate poisoning victim with excessive bronchial secretions.
back:
* Aggressive Atropine sulfate therapy.
* Repeat 2mg doses intravenously every five minutes until secretions cease.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [In severe intoxication or chronic exposure, aggressive and large doses of atropine are needed. Atropine sulfate is repeated intravenously at five minute intervals until toxic symptoms of atropine become manifest]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the maximum recommended insertion depth of a stomach tube in an adult victim?
back:
* 20 inches (50 cm).
* Corresponds to the average distance from mouth to the cardiac end of the stomach.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [Average distance between mouth and cardiac end of stomach is 18 inches (45 cm), therefore, tube must not be pushed in beyond this mark (20 inches).]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the primary objective of a "psychological autopsy" in forensic practice?
back: To determine the deceased's mental status at the precise time of their death, particularly in cases of alleged suicide.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Psychological autopsy is special exercise in case of alleged suicide. It is to know deceased's mental status at the time of his death.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Why is evaluating mental status prioritized in sexual assault examinations?
back: Forensic assessment is essential because these assaults frequently cause significantly more psychological damage than physical trauma.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [evaluation of mental status is both essential and important as such assaults cause more psychological damage than physical trauma]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Contrast the emotional state versus the psychomotor responses of a sexual assault victim.
back:
Emotional: Tense, withdrawn, and depressed.
Psychomotor: Retarded responses, thought blocks, and concentration disturbances.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [victim especially female is mostly depressed and may entertain suicidal ideas. Psychomotor responses in such a case are retarded with disturbance of concentration of mind.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: A victim exhibits retarded psychomotor responses and suicidal ideation post-assault. Interpret her likely status.
back: This represents a severe psychological trauma common in forcible sexual assault (zina-bil-jabr), often resulting in clinical depression.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [In case of sexual assaults, victim especially female is mostly depressed and may entertain suicidal ideas. Psychomotor responses in such a case are retarded]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: What is the relationship between painful recall and narration reluctance in assault victims?
back: Reluctance to narrate the incident is an emotional defense mechanism because the mental recall of the trauma is intensely painful.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [She may become reluctant to narrate the incidence, as recall is painful and requires, support and encouragement to overcome this feeling.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: List the primary sources for collecting data during a psychological autopsy.
back: Information is gathered from family members, friends, teachers, professional colleagues, and the victim's personal physician.
citation: Page 113 (Book Page): [Sources for collection of this information are family members, teachers, friends, professional colleagues and his physician]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: How is "thought block" interpreted by the examiner during a victim's interview?
back: It is interpreted as a manifestation of confusion and psychological trauma where the victim cannot express the specific allegation.
citation: Page 110 (Book Page): [Victim may be confused showing thought block and may feel difficulty in expressing even the allegation.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: A victim presents with a "drunken gait" and "ataxia." Differentiate the forensic concern.
back: The examiner must differentiate acute alcohol intoxication (Phase 2 confusion) from head injuries or metabolic disorders like hypoglycemia.
citation: Page 178 (Book Page): [Second is the stage of confusion... drunken gait and ataxia.] Page 180 (Book Page): [Differential diagnosis of alcohol intoxication (Conditions simulating alcohol intoxication) 1. Head injuries... 2. Metabolic disorders]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Explain the psychological transition an intoxicated victim undergoes during Phase II.
back: Depression of higher cortical centers leads to loss of inhibition, emotional upset, and coordination failure (confusion stage).
citation: Page 178 (Book Page): [Second is the stage of confusion... depression of the higher centers frees lower centers from cortical control... coordination may be marked.]

category: Interpret Psycho-pathology of victim
front: Q: Which specific clinic sub-specialty manages the analysis of victim psycho-pathology?
back: The Forensic Psychiatry department, situated within the specialized Medico-Legal Clinic.
citation: Page 9 (Book Page): [Forensic Psychiatry [located in] MEDICO LEGAL CLINIC]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What three specific conditions negate an assailant's criminal responsibility under legal exception?
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Exception negates criminal responsibility of the accused and is also three. They are immaturity, insanity or intoxication at the time of commission of crime.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Describe the "Irresistible Impulse" (Policeman at the shoulder) rule regarding an assailant’s pathology.
back: It posits that the assailant, due to a disease of the mind, would have committed the illegal act even if a law enforcement officer was standing directly beside them.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Irresistible Impulse also known as ‘Policeman at the shoulder’ meaning that the defendant, by reasons of disease of mind, would have acted as he did even had a policeman been standing at his side.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Differentiate between Sadism and Masochism as abnormal psychopathological sexual behaviors.
back:
* Sadism: Sexual pleasure derived from acts of cruelty to the partner.
* Masochism: Sexual pleasure derived from pain or injury inflicted by the partner.
citation: Page 34 (Book Page): [Sadism: Sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty to partner of opposite sex. Masochism: Sexual pleasure from pain/injury inflected by partner of the opposite sex.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Case: An assailant was sane during the crime but becomes insane before trial. Classify this verdict.
back:
* Verdict: Unfit to plead.
* Outcome: Court proceedings are suspended until the defendant's sanity is restored so they may defend themselves.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Unfit to plead, applicable when the defendant was sane at the time of commission of crime but has subsequently become insane and thus not capable of defending himself. The court proceeding gets suspended...]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What does the Latin term mens-rea connote in the context of criminal intent?
back: Connotes evil or criminal intent. It is a mandatory pre-requisite to guilt and a condition precedent to liability for a crime.
citation: Page 12 (Book Page): [Latin phrase mens-rea connotes evil or criminal intent, which is pre-requisite to guilt and thus a condition precedent to liability of the crime.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: List the three specific exceptions that negate the criminal responsibility of an accused assailant.
back: 1. Immaturity (child under ten years). 2. Insanity (adult with mental illness). 3. Involuntary intoxication (intake without knowledge or will).
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Exception negates criminal responsibility of the accused and is also three. They are immaturity, insanity or intoxication at the time of commission of crime.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Contrast the McNaughton Rules with the Durham Rule regarding the insanity defense.
back: McNaughton Rules focus on the defendant's capacity to make moral judgments. Durham Rule is based purely on medical concepts where the act is a product of mental disease.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [In contrast to the McNaughton’s Rules, which takes into account the defendant's capacity to make moral judgment, the Durham Rule is based on purely medical concepts.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Clinical Scenario: An assailant claims he could not stop himself from committing a crime despite a policeman standing next to him. Which rule applies?
back: Irresistible Impulse Rule (also known as 'Policeman at the shoulder'). It supplements McNaughton's Rules by addressing acts driven by mental disease despite awareness.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Americans have supplemented the MeNaughton’s Rules by “Irresistible Impulse” also known as ‘Policeman at the shoulder’ meaning that the defendant, by reasons of disease of mind, would have acted as he did even had a policeman been standing at his side.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define the legal requirements of the McNaughton Rules for a plea of insanity.
back: 1. Defect of reason due to disease of mind. 2. Failure to know the nature and quality of the action. 3. Failure to know the action was wrong.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Defect of reason was due to disease of mind. Due to disease of mind, i. He did not know nature and quality of his action ii. If he did know nature and quality of his action, he did not know, he was doing wrong.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: What is the defining characteristic of 'Sadism' in a sexual assailant?
back: The assailant derives sexual pleasure or gratification from performing acts of cruelty on a partner of the opposite sex.
citation: Page 31 (Book Page): [Sadism: Sexual pleasure from acts of cruelty to partner of opposite sex.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Explain the legal outcome for an assailant found to have 'Diminished Responsibility' during a trial.
back: The defendant is not completely absolved of guilt, but the severity of their sentence is mitigated or reduced due to mental impairment.
citation: Page 11 (Book Page): [Diminished responsibility is applicable to defendant who is not absolved completely, but the severity of his sentence gets mitigated or reduced.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Differentiate between Organic and Psychogenic Amnesia in an assailant with head trauma.
back: Organic: Result of brain pathology (trauma/degeneration) affecting registration and retention. Psychogenic: Result of psychological stress causing interference in recall (forgetting).
citation: Page 89 (Book Page): [Organic amnesia results from pathological changes in the brain... Psychogenic amnesia, on the other hand, occurs in situations of psychological stress causing interference in the process of recall.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: In the legal 'loop' of establishing a crime, what must accompany mens-rea to constitute a committed offense?
back: Actus-reus (evil action). In the absence of either mens-rea (intent) or actus-reus (action), a crime cannot be considered committed.
citation: Page 12 (Book Page): [Latin phrase actus-reus represents evil action. In absence of either of the two, the crime cannot be considered as committed.]

category: Interpret psycho-pathology of assailant
front: Q: Define 'Masochism' as a specific psychopathological sexual behavior.
back: The individual derives sexual pleasure from pain or injury inflicted upon them by a partner of the opposite sex.
citation: Page 31 (Book Page): [Masochism: Sexual pleasure from pain/injury inflicted by partner of the opposite sex.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Under what specific condition can a medico-legal examination duty be referred to another facility?
back: Only with permission of higher authorities. Transfer is otherwise inadvisable to prevent loss of vital evidence (e.g., in sexual assaults) and trauma masking due to repair.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [This duty can neither be referred to other medical facility without permission of higher authorities nor its examination delayed at authorized center. Transportation outside... is even inadvisable, because of chances for loss of vital evidence during transit].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What are the four primary clinical criteria used to assess the severity of acute poisoning?
back:
1. Degree of coma
2. Depth of respiratory depression
3. Extent of shock
4. Severity of hypothermia
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [Assessment of patient’s condition, regarding severity of acute poisoning should be done clinically from degree of coma, depth of respiratory depression, extent of shock and hypothermia].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How should a comatose patient be positioned for gastric lavage to prevent aspiration?
back: Prone lying position with face hanging over the table edge. This ensures the pharynx is lower than the larynx, preventing regurgitation into the air passages.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [Unconscious patient is placed on the table in prone lying position with his face downward hanging over the end of the table. Pharynx... would be at a lower level than the larynx and trachea and fluid leakage or regurgitation into larynx does not occur].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the recommended dosage and administration protocol for Naloxone in adult narcotic overdoses?
back: 0.4-0.8 mg/kg body weight IV or IM. Repeat at 2-3 minute intervals for three doses or more in severe cases.
citation: Page 169 (Book Page): [Adults, repeating the dose at two or three minute intervals for three doses. However, in severe cases a much larger dose may be required... 0.4-0.8 mg/kg body weight].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Contrast the use of Apomorphine and Syrup Ipecac in managing ingested poisons.
back: Apomorphine causes rapid projected vomiting but may induce shock. Syrup Ipecac is safer but carries a 15-minute delay in onset.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [Using emetics to induce vomiting. Apomorphine cause projected vomiting and shock. Syrup ipecac has its advantage, but there is delay of 15 minutes].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the preferred method for correcting central hypothermia in acute poisoning cases?
back: Warming the inspired air. This is the most effective way to address central hypothermia which contributes to shock, acidemia, and hypoxia.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [Best way to treat hypothermia is to rise the temperature of inspired air. Maintaining of tissue perfusion especially of brain, heart, lungs, liver and kidneys would treat shock].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Clinical Scenario: A victim of criminal assault is dying. What is the physician's immediate legal duty?
back: Record a Dying Declaration. The attending physician must not shrink this duty as they are the best judge of the victim's physical and mental state.
citation: Page 13 (Book Page): [Medical Practitioner in attendance and in-charge of such a patient would be the logical choice to record dying declaration. He should not shrink this legal duty].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How is shock clinically managed in acute poisoning to maintain vital organ perfusion?
back: If systolic BP < 80 mmHg, raise the foot of the bed and administer 3 mg Aromine IM at 20-minute intervals while correcting acidemia with bicarbonates.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [If systolic blood pressure is below 80 mm Hg... Raising foot of bed, aromine 3 mg intramuscularly at 20 minutes interval and correction of acidemia by infusion of bicarbonates].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: A victim presents with suspected organophosphate poisoning. Detail the Atropine Sulfate management protocol.
back: Administer 2 mg IV test dose initially. Increase and repeat doses frequently until respiratory secretions cease.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [In case of organo-phosphate poisoning, a test dose of 2 mg intravenously should be administered... The dosage of atropine sulfate must be increased and repeated frequently until cessation of secretion].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the required distance/marking for inserting a stomach tube in an average adult?
back: Insert up to the 20-inch (50 cm) mark. The distance from the mouth to the cardiac end of the stomach is approximately 18 inches (45 cm).
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [There is a mark at 20 inches (50 cm) from the lower end. Average distance between mouth and cardiac end of stomach is 18 inches (45 cm), therefore, tube must not be pushed in beyond this mark].

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Who is legally authorized to undertake a forensic medical examination of a living victim?
back: Only a formally authorized medical examiner is permitted to conduct the examination and issue forensic certification.
citation: Page 6 (Book Page): [Only authorized medical examiner to undertake forensic medical examination]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Why is the transportation of sexual assault victims to distant medical facilities discouraged?
back: It risks the loss of vital trace evidence during transit, through the call of nature, or accidental cleansing of parts.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [Transportation outside to other medical facility is even inadvisable, because of chances for loss of vital evidence during transit, call of nature, cleansing of parts especially in sexual assaults.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Distinguish between 'Implied' and 'Expressed' consent in the initial management of victims.
back:
• Implied: Applicable in emergencies (e.g., profuse bleeding) to prevent delay.
• Expressed: Required for non-emergencies; can be oral or written (written preferred).
citation: Page 21 (Book Page): [Implied consent is applicable in cases of medical emergency... Expressed consent is taken from all other cases than medical emergency.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Management Scenario: A forensic victim requires immediate life-saving surgery but refuses consent. Action?
back:
• Obtain advice from a senior colleague.
• Document the necessity and procedure in case notes.
• Proceed with essential treatment in good faith.
citation: Page 22 (Book Page): [In such situation medical practitioner should obtained advice of a senior colleague and enters in case notes and then proceeds with medical treatment.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the mandatory first step in managing a victim of ingested poison upon hospital arrival?
back: Immediate gastric lavage (stomach wash) is essential to remove unabsorbed poison, even if the victim has already vomited.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [It is first thing to be done on receipt of patient in hospital. Speed is essential. It is done nearly in all cases of ingested poison]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: List three administrative prerequisites required before initiating a forensic medical examination.
back:
1. Expressed written consent.
2. Verification of personal identity (CNIC).
3. Record of examination fee (amount and recipient).
citation: Page 6 (Book Page): [Expressed written consent of examinee, a prerequisite. Verification of examinee’s personal identity essential. Who, how much and to whom fee of medical examination paid be recorded for transparence]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How must clothing be removed from a victim to preserve trace evidence like hair or fibers?
back: The victim must stand on a plain white sheet and undress unaided to prevent the loss of falling particles.
citation: Page 101 (Book Page): [Examination of clothes should be done making the examinee stand on plain white cloth free from any contamination. Undressing should be done unaided by the examinee herself]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How is 'Temporary Reception' managed for a mentally ill victim requiring admission?
back:
