• Application by a blood or marriage relative.
• Supported by two medical certificates from RMPs.
• Valid for 14 days from the date of issue.
citation: Page 18 (Book Page): [Temporary reception is grant upon submission of a formal application... by a relative... supported with two medical certificates... valid only unto 14 days from the date of issue.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Why is gastric lavage performed despite prior vomiting in acute poisoning cases?
back: Vomiting is often incomplete; lavage ensures the maximum removal of residual unabsorbed poison from the gastric mucosa.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [It should be done even after vomiting, which supposedly have removed all stomach contents.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the recommended architectural facility for managing living forensic victims?
back: A dedicated 'Medico-legal clinic' equipped with resuscitation, sterilization, and purpose-built examination tools.
citation: Page 8 (Book Page): [What is recommended that architecturally-designed centers having medico-legal clinic for examination of living forensic cases... should be provided]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Under what specific condition can a medico-legal examination be referred to another medical facility?
back:
* Only with the expressed permission of higher authorities.
* Transportation is otherwise inadvisable to prevent loss of vital evidence or trauma masking.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [This duty can neither be referred to other medical facility without permission of higher authorities nor its examination delayed at authorized center. Transportation outside... is even inadvisable, because of chances for loss of vital evidence]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Why is immediate initial management critical for trauma victims in forensic cases?
back:
* Prevents masking of injuries by natural repair or infection.
* Avoids evidence loss via cleansing (sexual assaults).
* Prevents changes caused by corpse decomposition.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [Further findings in trauma cases with lapse of time get masked due to onset of repair or infection in the injured part and decomposition of the corpse.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How does forensic sample management contrast with routine clinical laboratory procedures?
back:
* Forensic: Requires maintaining a strict chain of custody.
* Forensic: Requires a low threshold of suspicion regarding history and potential substitution.
* Forensic: Sampling must be under personal medical supervision.
citation: Page 6 (Book Page): [Forensic Medical Examiner has to entertain low threshold of suspicion, while evaluating history of allegation... and maintains chain of custody of forensic samples]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the priority clinical management step for a suspected acute poisoning victim?
back:
* Maintain a clear airway (highest priority).
* Assist pulmonary ventilation and provide oxygen.
* Treat shock, pain, or convulsions as necessary.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [The following principles are adopted; maintain the airway clear, assist pulmonary ventilation, give oxygen when necessary, treat shock and pain and sedate if the patient is convulsive.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Which fluid is the primary choice for initial gastric irrigation when a poison's identity is unknown?
back:
* Pure warm water.
* Administer 1-2 cups for children and 3-5 cups for adults.
* Avoid excessive quantities to prevent premature pyloric relaxation and absorption.
citation: Page 169 (Book Page): [Water is the best and indeed the only fluid, which is used especially when the identity of the poison is not known... administer one to two cups-full to a child and three to five cups-full to an adult.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: List the three mandatory pre-requisites before starting a forensic medical examination.
back:
* Expressed written consent of the examinee.
* Verification of the examinee's personal identity.
* Documentation of the requesting authority (Police/Court).
citation: Page 6 (Book Page): [Table 1.1: Expressed written consent of examinee, a prerequisite; Verification of examinee’s personal identity essential; On whose behalf i.e. examinee’s, police or law court]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How must a medical practitioner manage an emergency victim who is unable to consent?
back:
* Apply the doctrine of implied consent.
* Obtain advice and endorsement from a senior colleague.
* Fully document all procedures and circumstances in case notes.
citation: Page 20 (Book Page): [Implied consent is applicable in cases of medical emergency... Page 22 (Book Page): medical practitioner should obtained advice of a senior colleague and enters in case notes and then proceeds with medical treatment.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What documentation must accompany a victim referred for forensic laboratory analysis?
back:
* Fully documented positive and negative findings.
* Chain of custody labels for all exhibits.
* Signed and stamped descriptions of clothing and physical status.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [Findings both positive as well as negative should be documented... Other details such as description of worn clothes... are included in the medical certificate.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: What is the absolute priority in the initial management of a trauma victim?
back: Start medical treatment immediately. Do not waste time for consent formalities in medical emergencies (implied consent).
citation: Page 17 (Book Page): [no time should be wasted in starting medical treatment. It should be started immediately condoning the formality of consent taking.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Explain the role of 'implied consent' in the initial management of trauma victims.
back: Used in emergencies where serious injuries (e.g., profuse bleeding) prevent verbal consent; allows immediate life-saving intervention without legal delay.
citation: Page 17 (Book Page): [Implied consent is applicable in cases of medical emergency... no time should be wasted in starting medical treatment.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Contrast the referral of forensic cases with routine clinical referrals regarding jurisdiction.
back: Forensic duty cannot be referred to other facilities without permission from higher authorities; transport is discouraged to prevent evidence loss.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [This duty can neither be referred to other medical facility without permission of higher authorities nor its examination delayed at authorized center.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Why is immediate referral of a sexual assault victim to an unauthorized facility clinically inadvisable?
back: High risk of losing vital trace evidence through cleansing or transit; authorized centers ensure legal and forensic integrity.
citation: Page 7 (Book Page): [Transportation outside to other medical facility is even inadvisable, because of chances for loss of vital evidence during transit, call of nature, cleansing of parts especially in sexual assaults.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Which clinical vitals must be stabilized in initial management before detailed forensic examination?
back: Maintain a clear airway, assist ventilation, provide oxygen, and treat shock and pain to ensure victim survival.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [maintain the airway clear, assist pulmonary ventilation, give oxygen when necessary, treat shock and pain and sedate if the patient is convulsive.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: List the primary life-saving interventions for a patient received in hospital with acute poisoning.
back: Clear the airway, provide oxygen/ventilation, treat shock, and perform gastric lavage unless contraindicated (e.g., corrosives).
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [maintain the airway clear, assist pulmonary ventilation, give oxygen when necessary, treat shock and pain.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How should a physician manage the referral protocol for a suspected criminal abortion victim facing imminent death?
back: Record a dying declaration immediately; report the case to police upon death and withhold the certificate until autopsy.
citation: Page 98 (Book Page): [patient should be encouraged to record a dying declaration if death seems imminent. Upon death of patient, matter should be reported to police immediately and certificate of cause of death withheld till conduction of autopsy.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: How is the clinical severity of acute poisoning assessed during initial hospital management?
back: Based on the depth of coma (Stages 1-4), depth of respiratory depression, and extent of shock/hypothermia.
citation: Page 170 (Book Page): [Assessment of patient’s condition, regarding severity of acute poisoning should be done clinically from degree of coma, depth of respiratory depression, extent of shock and hypothermia.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Describe the protective posture required for an unconscious patient during initial gastric lavage.
back: Prone lying position with face hanging over the table; ensures the pharynx is lower than the larynx to prevent aspiration.
citation: Page 168 (Book Page): [Unconscious patient is placed on the table in prone lying position with his face downward hanging over the end of the table. Pharynx of patient in this position would be at a lower level than the larynx.]

category: Plan initial management & referral of victim
front: Q: Which clinical specimens must be prioritized during the initial management of a poisoning referral?
back: Stomach wash (first 500cc), 10cc blood (without spirit swabs), and entire available quantity of urine.
citation: Page 160 (Book Page): [Stomach wash at least 500cc... blood... at least 10-cc from a peripheral vein... Urine... entire quantity available.]
